requirement: When BorderArrangement arranges a layout under a fixed-width AND fixed-height constraint (the arrangeFF path) and a right block is present, the right block is arranged with a width Range whose upper bound is the larger of (constraint width minus the arranged width of the left block) and 0.0; consequently, if the available width is so small that the left block already occupies all of it (or more), the right block's allowed width is clamped to a non-negative leftover (0.0) rather than being given a negative upper width bound, so the arrangement completes without throwing or placing the right block under a bogus negative-width constraint.

When a DefaultIntervalCategoryDataset is constructed with non-null but zero-series start/end arrays (e.g. empty double[][]/Number[][] data), the constructor stores its series-keys and category-keys as zero-length (empty) arrays rather than as null, so that the key/lookup accessors that read those arrays operate normally instead of throwing: getRowCount() and getColumnCount() return 0, getSeriesIndex()/getRowIndex() and getCategoryIndex()/getColumnIndex() return -1 for any argument, and getRowKeys()/getColumnKeys() return (an) empty list rather than raising a NullPointerException.

KeyedObjects2D.getObject(rowKey, columnKey): after both keys are validated as present at the table level, if the specific row's backing KeyedObjects data contains no entry for columnKey (getIndex < 0), the method returns null rather than delegating to KeyedObjects.getObject(columnKey) (which would throw UnknownKeyException for such a missing cell).

In Axis.drawLabel, when plotState is non-null and the label's hotspot has been computed (non-null), but plotState.getOwner() returns null, the method does not throw a NullPointerException; it skips the axis-label entity registration and returns the axis state normally.

In PosixParser.flatten, for a "--"-prefixed token whose long-option name IS a defined option (or, when stopAtNonOption is false, regardless of whether the name is a defined option), the token is decomposed into its name and value tokens: when the token contains an '=', the result is the name token "--opt" followed by the substring after the first '=' as a separate value token; when it contains no '=', the whole token is emitted as a single name token.

When HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText needs to wrap text over multiple lines (i.e. the first line itself was wrapped) and the supplied nextLineTabStop is greater than or equal to the supplied width, the method must not throw an IllegalStateException and must still complete, producing a wrapped result instead of aborting.

Util.stripLeadingAndTrailingQuotes removes one leading and one trailing double quote and returns the interior text when (and only when) the input has length >= 2, begins with a double quote, ends with a double quote, and contains no double quote in the characters strictly between the endpoints (e.g. '"foo"' -> 'foo').

HelpFormatter.findWrapPos chops an overlong run of text at exactly column startPos+width: when no whitespace (space, '\n', or '\r') occurs anywhere in the window from startPos up to startPos+width (i.e., text there is a continuous non-whitespace run) and startPos+width is within the string (startPos+width < text.length()), findWrapPos returns startPos+width as the wrap position rather than advancing forward to the next whitespace character located beyond startPos+width.

printWrapped separates the individual source lines of a multi-line input in its output using the newline configured on the HelpFormatter (getNewLine()/setNewLine), i.e. each source line is terminated/joined with the configured platform line separator regardless of the specific line terminator sequence used to separate lines in the input.
TypeHandler.openFile(String str) returns a FileInputStream opened on the file at the given path when that file exists and can be opened.

TypeHandler.createValue(String, Class<T>) throws a ParseException whose message is "Unable to handle the class: " followed by the string form of the given clazz when clazz matches none of the PatternOptionBuilder sentinel values recognized by the method (STRING_VALUE, OBJECT_VALUE, NUMBER_VALUE, DATE_VALUE, CLASS_VALUE, FILE_VALUE, EXISTING_FILE_VALUE, FILES_VALUE, URL_VALUE), rather than returning null.

When RemoveUnusedVars is run with removeGlobals=false, it does not remove/bare any formal parameters of functions it visits: unreferenced function arguments are left in place in every function declaration (the trailing-unreferenced-argument stripping step is skipped), and no call sites are modified for function-argument removal. Function-argument removal (peeling unreferenced trailing formals, and any call-site optimization of argument lists) occurs only when the pass is run with removeGlobals=true.
The mayBeString(Node, boolean) non-recursive path (recurse=false), which delegates directly to mayBeStringHelper, is left unchanged by the fix.

JSDoc type-annotation alias expansion (e.g. rewriting an alias base name such as 'sub.C' to its expanded target) is applied to each goog.scope body's own original annotations independently of any injected ($jscomp.scope) copies that were produced earlier within the same or a previous goog.scope block; tracking used to deduplicate the jsdoc processing of injected declarations is cleared when leaving each top-level goog.scope scope rather than persisting across distinct goog.scope blocks.

When a function declaration inside a goog.scope body is rewritten, the original named 'function <name>(){}' statement is replaced: the function's name child is removed (made anonymous, to avoid an IE global-name leak) and the resulting anonymous function expression is emitted as the value of the generated '$jscomp.scope.<name>' declaration, replacing the prior location of the function declaration in the output.

When processing a global-scope assignment whose LHS is a tracked name, if that assignment node is the first (callee) child of a CALL node — i.e. the assigned value is used directly as the function being invoked — NameAnalyzer records no dependency scope tying the assignment's subtree to the LHS name. Consequently global names referenced inside that assignment (e.g. within the body of the assigned function being called) are not classified as existing only because the LHS name is referenced, so they remain kept/referenced and are not removed even when the LHS name itself is unreferenced (e.g. in `var fun, x; (fun = function(){ x; })();` the reference to `x` is preserved while the now-unreferenced alias `fun` is removed).

When TypeCheck visits a `new X(...)` expression whose constructor's type, after restrictByNotNullOrUndefined, is classified as a constructor/empty/unknown type AND resolves to a non-null FunctionType that reports no instance type (fnType.hasInstanceType() == false), TypeCheck does not proceed down the normal-constructor path; instead it falls into the fallback that leaves the NEW node typed only via ensureTyped (i.e. it does not dereference/getInstanceType of that FunctionType or validate the argument list against its parameters).

For a try statement with a finally clause, MinimizeExitPoints' exit-minimization does not remove or rewrite explicit exits (matching returns, breaks, or continues, per the current exitType/labelName context) that appear inside the finally block: statements within the finally clause are left unchanged by this pass.

When an unconditional control-flow jump — an argument-less return, a break, or a continue — is otherwise eligible for removal (its single branch target equals its computed fall-through/follow node, so that removing it would preserve control flow), UnreachableCodeElimination must NOT remove it if that jump statement is lexically contained within the body of the finally clause of any enclosing try statement. The jump is preserved in the (nominally unchanged) output regardless of how deeply it is nested inside the finally body, including within nested (multi-level) finally blocks.

When the retraversal pass iterates over the children of a node, a child's subtree optimization (which may structurally mutate the tree, detaching or rewriting nodes) must not affect which sibling is processed next: the caller's iteration continues from the sibling that followed the child before the child was traversed, so no original sibling is skipped or revisited and the loop makes forward progress to a fixed point.

TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(String s) returns false for any non-null input string that contains at least one character c for which Character.isIdentifierIgnorable(c) returns true, regardless of whether that character is the first character of the string or appears later.

InlineRenamer registers a hard invariant that it is never asked to add "arguments" as a declared name: InlineRenamer.addDeclaredName("arguments") throws an IllegalStateException rather than planning any rename for the special arguments binding.

When the --version flag is supplied, CommandLineRunner writes a version banner to the configured error stream and flushes it, emitted before any help/usage output; the banner text is 'Closure Compiler (http://code.google.com/p/closure/compiler)\n' followed by 'Version: <ParserConfig.compiler.version>\n' and 'Built on: <ParserConfig.compiler.date>', where the two values are read from the com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.ParserConfig resource bundle.

When CompilerOptions.checkSymbols is false but the warning guards already installed on the supplied CompilerOptions (options.getWarningsGuard as populated, e.g. via setWarningLevel(DiagnosticGroups.CHECK_VARIABLES, ...)/addWarningsGuard called before init) enable the CHECK_VARIABLES diagnostic group, Compiler.initOptions does NOT append a CHECK_VARIABLES-OFF suppression guard, so undefined-variable (VarCheck.UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR) and multiply-declared-variable (SyntacticScopeCreator.VAR_MULTIPLY_DECLARED_ERROR) diagnostics emitted by the variable-check pass are reported at the level configured by the user rather than being silenced.

JSType.isInvariant(other) returns true whenever at least one of the two types is the unknown type: under the invariance check the unknown type is treated as invariant (compatible) with any type, so a pair whose one member is unknown is not disqualified on that account.

An input file that parses cleanly (its parse adds no new errors to the compiler error manager) retains its parsed AST even when some earlier input had already reported parse/halting errors; the empty-script (`IR.script()`) dummy fallback no longer triggers merely because of pre-existing errors from other inputs.

In DIRECT inlining mode, a call is refused (NO) when an argument expression itself carries mutable state (may effect mutable state) and its corresponding parameter is referenced at all in the function body—even a single time—because the argument would have to be aliased into a temporary to be safe.

When a variable is declared with an explicitly declared (non-inferred) type and its initializer expression's inferred type is the void/undefined type, the in-flow type of that variable after the declaration statement is the void/undefined type (not the declared type), so subsequent uses in that scope are type-checked against undefined rather than against the declared type.

During source setup (parseInputs), dependency management runs whenever options.dependencyOptions.needsManagement() is true, regardless of whether options.closurePass is enabled: each input's provided types are forward-declared in the type registry and inputs are re-sorted so that they satisfy their required/provided reordering.

When options.closurePass is enabled and dependencyOptions.needsManagement() is true, dependency management (forward-declaring provided types and re-ordering/dropping the source inputs per the managed-dependency ordering and entry points) runs during parse regardless of whether options.skipAllPasses is set; consequently, with skipAllPasses enabled, the ordered/filtered set of source inputs (as reflected in the resulting source output / input ordering) reflects dependency-based re-ordering and removal rather than the original input order.

When the result of an assignment expression is dropped/not needed by its enclosing code (so the assigned value does not escape via that assignment), a variable with only such assignments and a property/element assignment remains removable rather than being flagged as escaped and kept.

During Compiler.initOptions, the GLOBAL_THIS diagnostic group's check level is set equal to options.checkGlobalThisLevel if and only if that checkGlobalThisLevel is on AND the GLOBAL_THIS diagnostic group is not explicitly disabled by the options' warnings guard (options.disables(DiagnosticGroups.GLOBAL_THIS) is false); in particular, when the GLOBAL_THIS group is explicitly disabled, initOptions leaves it disabled rather than forcing it back on to options.checkGlobalThisLevel.

AnalyzePrototypeProperties treats a chained prototype-property assignment of the form X.prototype.p = <value> (a simple '=' assignment whose LHS is a GETPROP chain of the form ...'.prototype.p') as a prototype-property assignment only when that assignment node is the direct child of a bare expression statement (it appears standalone, as in 'Foo.prototype.bar = function(){...};'). When such a chained prototype assignment occurs in some other syntactic position (its parent is not an expression statement, e.g. nested inside another statement or expression), it is no longer recognized as a prototype-property assignment, so the traversal does not analyze the assigned value within the context of the property p it defines.

When CollapseProperties collapses a global property whose single-declaration value is a FUNCTION (handled by updateSimpleDeclaration), and that function's body references `this`, and the function's recording JSDoc (the name's docInfo) is neither a @constructor nor declares a @this type, the compiler reports an UNSAFE_THIS (JSC_UNSAFE_THIS) diagnostic for each such `this` occurrence, labeled with the property's full name.

When validating a function's @this type for the THIS_TYPE_NON_OBJECT check ('@this type of a function must be an object'), null and undefined are stripped from the given type before testing whether it is a subtype of Object, so a @this type that contains null/undefined alongside an actual object type (e.g. an optional/nullable type) is accepted (no JSC_THIS_TYPE_NON_OBJECT warning is reported), and the warning is reported only if the @this type's value portion after removing null/undefined is still not an object subtype.

isValidDefineValue recognizes expressions built from the binary operators + (ADD), - (SUB), * (MUL), / (DIV), % (MOD), < (LT), <= (LE), > (GT), >= (GE), == (EQ), != (NE), === (SHEQ), !== (SHNE), << (LSH), >> (RSH), >>> (URSH) as valid define values when both operands are themselves valid define values; previously none of these operator nodes was recognized and they all evaluated to false/invalid.

When type-checking a CALL or NEW against a function type whose last formal parameter is a var_args ('@param {...T}') parameter, every actual argument that has no corresponding fixed declared parameter is type-checked against that var_args parameter's type rather than being silently skipped: once all fixed (non-varargs) declared parameters have been consumed, each remaining actual argument is still matched against the retained var_args parameter while arguments remain.

combine(ExtendedProperties) copies into the receiver (this) each entry yielded by props.getKeys(), placing the exact value object retrieved via props.get(key) without any ExtendedProperties value-processing: no backslash-unescaping, comma tokenization, or String→List/Vector conversion is applied to copied values. As a result, after combine, getProperty(key) on the receiver returns a value equivalent to the raw stored value in props (e.g. a String containing multiple consecutive backslashes is preserved unchanged rather than being unescaped again as setProperty's addProperty would do).

TarArchiveOutputStream.writePaxHeaders constructs its PAX extended-header entry name from './PaxHeaders.X/' + the 7-bit-stripped entry name and strips every trailing '/' character from that reconstructed name before applying the header-name truncation, so the resulting PAX header entry name never ends in '/'.

When reading a new-format entry whose header c_mode has zero file-type bits (mode & S_IFMT == 0) and whose name is not "TRAILER!!!", CpioArchiveInputStream throws an IOException (message "Mode 0 only allowed in the trailer..."), regardless of whether the mode word itself is exactly zero or merely lacks file-type bits.

Byte production for a decoded block is initiated lazily on the read path rather than during construction: a freshly-constructed stream whose decoder is positioned at START_BLOCK_STATE yields its first decompressed byte on the first read() call (START_BLOCK_STATE is serviced by performing block output setup and returning its byte), rather than having block output set up and a pending byte buffered ahead of time by the constructor.

When reading data from the current tar entry, if the underlying input stream signals EOF by returning -1 while the requested read length (numToRead, already capped by the current entry's remaining available bytes) is greater than 0, then read(byte[],int,int) throws an IOException whose message is "Truncated TAR archive", rather than silently recording end-of-archive.

verifyCheckSum can propagate an IllegalArgumentException thrown by parseOctal when the trimmed CHKSUM-field content contains a byte that is neither an octal digit nor leading/trailing space/NUL padding (a field the previous lenient digit-scan never rejected) rather than merely returning false.

TarArchiveEntry.isDirectory() returns false for an entry whose file is null and whose linkFlag is neither LF_DIR nor a PAX/global-PAX extended header flag, is not a directory by other means, even when its name ends in "/"...

After reading the next local file header signature from a non-first entry (or the shifted first header), if that signature is neither the Local File Header signature (LFH), the Central File Header signature (CFH) nor the Archive Extra Data signature (AED), getNextZipEntry throws a java.util.zip.ZipException whose message contains the offending signature value formatted as '0X%X' (hex), instead of returning null.

Each Date-based setter (setModifyJavaTime, setAccessJavaTime, setCreateJavaTime) throws IllegalArgumentException when the supplied Date's seconds-since-epoch value (its millis / 1000) falls outside the signed 32-bit integer range (i.e., is < Integer.MIN_VALUE or > Integer.MAX_VALUE); a value within that range is accepted without throwing.
CSVFormat.EXCEL has allowMissingColumnNames set to true, i.e. calling EXCEL.getAllowMissingColumnNames() returns true (previously it returned false).
CSVFormat.MYSQL is configured with the null string equal to the literal two-character text "\N" (backslash followed by N): getNullString() returns "\\N" and isNullStringSet() returns true.

In CSVFormat#printAndQuote's QuoteMode.MINIMAL branch (the effective mode when getQuoteMode() is null) with quoting enabled, when the printed value begins a new record/line (newRecord is true), a value is no longer automatically wrapped in the quote character merely because its leading character is non-alphanumeric; instead such wrapping is forced at a value start only when the leading character is not a legal RFC4180 TEXTDATA printable character (i.e. is a control char < U+0020, is the double-quote U+0022, is the comma U+002C, or is > U+007E) or when the leading character is <= the comment-start character '#'. Consequently a first-column value whose leading character is an ordinary printable punctuation such as '-', '.', '!', '$', '(' or space prints without surrounding quotes when it contains no quote character, delimiter, CR/LF, or trailing-space char that independently forces quoting — e.g. a negative-number value like '-57' in the first column is emitted unquoted.

CSVPrinter.println() marks a new record (setting its internal new-record state true) so that a subsequent print() starts a fresh record without leading delimiter, even when the format's record separator is null and no separator characters are emitted.

TypeAdapters.NUMBER.read (used when deserializing to a Number-typed target, e.g. gson.fromJson("\"5\"", Number.class)) accepts a JSON STRING token and returns a Number representing that string's numeric value, instead of throwing a JsonSyntaxException — i.e. a quoted numeric string literal deserializes to a Number in the same way an unquoted NUMBER literal does.

A JSON generator's runtime toggling of the QUOTE_FIELD_NAMES feature is fully symmetric through the JsonGenerator enable()/disable() pair, so that after enable(Feature.QUOTE_FIELD_NAMES) and then disable(Feature.QUOTE_FIELD_NAMES), the quoting state of subsequently written field names returns to unquoted; disable(Feature.QUOTE_FIELD_NAMES) restores the unquoted behavior that a generator constructed with QUOTE_FIELD_NAMES disabled, and then enabled at runtime, would lose.

When a release sanity check fails because a different, strictly smaller buffer is being released, the thrown IllegalArgumentException carries message text 'Trying to release buffer smaller than original'.

When writeValue() is invoked on an object-type context at a point where no field name is pending (a field name has not just been written that expects a value, e.g., right after the object started), writeValue() returns STATUS_EXPECT_NAME and does not advance the object's field state, instead of returning STATUS_OK_AFTER_COLON as before.

In deserializeUsingPropertyBasedWithUnwrapped, once all remaining trailing fields after the last creator property have been copied into the unwrapped buffer, if the parser's current token is not END_OBJECT, deserialization fails by reporting a wrong-token mismatch against expected token END_OBJECT with a message of the form "Attempted to unwrap '<handled type name>' value" rather than proceeding to write the end-object token and process unwrapped content.

When a TreeTraversingParser is positioned on a numeric value that cannot be converted to an int (node.canConvertToInt() is false), calling getLongValue() does not silently return node.longValue() but reports a long overflow: it throws a JsonParseException (InputCoercionException subtype) naming the value and 'out of range of long'. Consequence of the guard used: numeric long/BigInteger values that fit in a long but exceed int range also trigger this long-overflow report, because the double/long range check used is canConvertToInt() rather than canConvertToLong(). For a value that can convert to int, getLongValue() returns the value unchanged.

Serializing a BigDecimal value whose property/type declares STRING format shape while JsonGenerator.Feature.WRITE_BIGDECIMAL_AS_PLAIN is ENABLED and whose scale is outside [-9999, 9999] (|scale| > 9999) fails with a JsonMappingException (via provider.reportMappingProblem) whose message names the offending scale and the [-9999, 9999] bound, rather than writing any output.

When an ObjectReader binds JSON content as a JSON tree (the _bindAsTree path, used by ObjectReader.readTree(...) and by tree reads issued through the reader acting as a parser codec, e.g. JsonParser.readValueAsTree()), the root deserializer it uses is one for the JsonNode type resolved from the deserialization context and cached keyed by that JsonNode type; it must NOT be the reader's prefetched _rootDeserializer whenever that prefetched deserializer corresponds to some other (non-JsonNode) value type configured on the reader. Consequently, even a reader configured for a concrete value type (e.g. via readerForUpdating(bean) or forType(beanCls), where EAGER_DESERIALIZER_FETCH prefetches the bean deserializer) still performs correct tree deserialization — producing a faithful JsonNode rather than driving that bean deserializer over the JSON, which for a bean with a nested custom subtree-consuming deserializer previously caused the child subtree to be mis-consumed/mis-attributed.
JavaType.isJavaLangObject() returns true if and only if the type's raw/erased class is java.lang.Object, and false for any other class (including subclasses like arrays, Strings, etc.).

MappingIterator.close() is an idempotent, terminal operation: the first call to close() closes the underlying parser (when one is present) and transitions the iterator into its closed state, after which subsequent close() calls, hasNextValue() calls, and nextValue() calls behave as on an exhausted iterator (no repeated access to a closed parser, hasNextValue() returns false, and nextValue() throws NoSuchElementException) rather than attempting further reads.

For an actual Map type (a java.util.Map implementation such as a class extending HashMap), the chosen serializer is, in order: a module-registered custom Map serializer if one matches, else an annotation-derived serializer (@JsonValue / JsonSerializable) if the class declares one, else the default Map serializer — so a module custom Map serializer overrides @JsonValue/JsonSerializable, and @JsonValue (e.g. a Map subclass whose @JsonValue method returns an int, serialized as that number) is still honored when no module serializer applies.

Calling BaseSettings.withDateFormat with a non-null DateFormat that differs (by reference) from the current _dateFormat returns a new BaseSettings whose reported TimeZone (getTimeZone()) is the same as the original settings' _timeZone, regardless of the timezone associated with the newly-supplied DateFormat (i.e. the DateFormat's own timezone must NOT override the config-level timezone).

TypeBindings.asKey(rawBase) returns an object encoding both the given raw class and this bindings' type parameters such that two returned keys are equal (and hash-equal) iff they were created from the same raw class and from bindings whose type-parameter sequences are pairwise equal; keys created from different parameter sequences for the same raw class, or from different raw classes, are unequal.

Deserializing a Locale String whose components are separated by hyphens at both boundaries — e.g. a string with two hyphens like "en-US-foo"/hyphen variant strings — yields a three-component Locale (language, country, variant), mirroring how a two-underscore string is parsed.

When a Reference's effective class (from _from, whether a Class value or an instance's runtime class) is an array type, the class-name segment rendered by getDescription() (and hence toString()) is the fully-qualified name of the array's innermost element/component class followed by one empty "[]" suffix per array dimension (e.g. an int[][].class reference yields "int[][]"; a String[].class reference yields "java.lang.String[]").

StdKeyDeserializer.forType recognizes CharSequence.class as a string-like key type (alongside String.class and Object.class) and returns a non-null StringKD key deserializer for it, instead of falling through to return null.

InnerClassProperty.getCreatorIndex() returns the creator index reported by the wrapped delegate property (the value of _delegate.getCreatorIndex()), so that for a wrapped creator-backed property the index returned is the delegate's non-negative creator index rather than the IllegalStateException that SettableBeanProperty.getCreatorIndex() throws for properties without an assigned creator index.

ObjectIdInfo.empty() returns a non-null, re-usable (single shared) ObjectIdInfo whose getAlwaysAsId() is false, whose getPropertyName() is an empty/no-name PropertyName, whose getGeneratorType() is null, whose getScope() is Object.class, and whose getResolverType() is non-null (resolved to the default resolver).

In refineSerializationType for a map/map-like type, when the explicit @JsonSerialize.keyAs value Class forms a primitive/wrapper pair with the key type's raw class (and is otherwise unrelated by inheritance), refinement must NOT throw a JsonMappingException; instead it must succeed, keeping the key's raw class and the returned map-like JavaType with the key's static typing forced.

ValueInstantiator.canInstantiate() returns true when canCreateUsingArrayDelegate() returns true, in addition to the pre-existing conditions (canCreateUsingDefault, canCreateUsingDelegate, canCreateFromObjectWith, canCreateFromString, canCreateFromInt, canCreateFromLong, canCreateFromDouble, canCreateFromBoolean).

SubTypeValidator.validateSubType does not apply the AbstractPointcutAdvisor/AbstractApplicationContext superclass-name scan to an interface type: an interface whose binary name starts with "org.springframework." is not rejected by that Spring name-scan rule (it passes validation unless otherwise matched by _cfgIllegalClassNames) rather than being scanned and crashing.
When the InputStream argument is null, writeBinary writes a null value (the empty/self-closing element appropriate to the current context) and returns 0.
A `:not(...)` selector whose parenthesized subselect is empty is rejected with an exception (the empty-argument case does not silently return the full result set).

In parseByteData charset auto-detection (charsetName argument null), when the selected first meta carries an http-equiv attribute whose content does not resolve to a charset via getCharsetFromContentType, and the same meta also has a charset attribute naming a supported charset (that does not throw IllegalCharsetNameException on the support check), that charset-attribute value is used to re-decode the document instead of keeping the initial default-UTF-8 decoding; an unsupported or illegal-name charset attribute is ignored and the default decoding is retained.

For self-closing start tags of the InBody rawtext elements (<noembed />, <iframe />, <xmp />) that reach handleRawtext, the tokenising mode used for the remainder of the document is the normal Data mode (not Rawtext), i.e. content and tags following such an element are not absorbed as raw element data by the closed element.

After an Element is cloned via clone(), a subsequent structural mutation of the clone's child-node list (for example appending a new descendant/sibling element) must invalidate and refresh the clone's own cached shadow child-elements list, so that element-tree queries that depend on that cache (e.g. nextElementSibling, previousElementSibling, children of the affected element) on the clone reflect the new child — behaving for later mutation queries the same as an equivalent independently-built element would.

A LeafNode (e.g. a TextNode or other leaf) now behaves as a node with zero child nodes for every Node operation that queries or traverses child nodes: child-enumeration operations that previously raised UnsupportedOperationException ('Leaf Nodes do not have child nodes.') from ensureChildNodes() now return/act on an empty child-node list instead — concretely childNodes() and childNodesCopy() return an empty list, childNode(index) accesses an empty list, and unwrap()/childNodesAsArray() treat the leaf as having no children rather than throwing.

When parseInputStream parses a document using a charset whose canEncode() is false, the document's charset/encoding metadata element (HTML <meta charset> or XML encoding declaration) is updated/inserted to declare the default charset (UTF-8), making the serialized declaration consistent with the document's output charset.

A Tag stores an always-lowercased 'normal name' computed at construction from the tag name via Normalizer.lowerCase(tagName), and exposes it publicly through Tag.normalName(). The normal name is independent of the tag's output/stored name (which may preserve case), so an unknown tag whose stored name retains input case (parse with preserveCase) still reports its lowercase normal name.

FormElement.formData() excludes a form control element from the returned key/value data when the element's type attribute is "button" (case-insensitively, e.g. "BUTTON"), even if that element is otherwise form-submittable, enabled, and named.

Calling getNamespaceResolver() on a DOMNodePointer returns a cached resolver instance: the same NamespaceResolver object is returned on every call; that resolver's namespace context pointer (getNamespaceContextPointer()) is the DOMNodePointer itself, and its parent resolver is the one obtained from the superclass (the enclosing/context NamespaceResolver).

In CoreOperationRelationalExpression.compute(Object left, Object right), when after reduction left is NOT an Iterator but right IS an Iterator, the operation's result is true iff the actual relational comparison (e.g. <, <=, >, >= as given by the operation's evaluateCompare) holds between the (non-iterator) left operand as the FIRST relation argument and at least one element yielded by the right iterator as the SECOND argument; otherwise the result is false (the operand order is no longer reversed).

PropertyPointer.getLength() returns 1 (instead of the 0 previously produced via ValueUtils.getLength(null)) when the underlying property value, getBaseValue(), is null, so that a property whose raw value is null is treated as spanning a single node rather than as an empty span.

DOMNodePointer.getNamespaceURI(Node node) returns null (rather than the empty string) whenever the resolved namespace URI for the node is the empty string — whether resolved via element.getNamespaceURI() or, when that returns null, via the nearest xmlns/xmlns:prefix attribute declaration found while walking up from the node through its enclosing elements.

When a cross-tree comparison reduces both pointers to their own distinct tree roots at the same depth (both at depth 1, non-null and not equal to each other), those two roots are treated as an ordering tie and the comparison returns 0 (rather than being treated as an error).

When a non-null chars array is supplied to RandomStringUtils.random with start==0 and end==0, the generated string's characters are drawn only from within that chars array (index range [0, chars.length)); in particular this no longer overflows the array bounds (previously could select arbitrary near-Integer.MAX_VALUE indices causing ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException), and with a single-element chars set the deterministic result is the repeated char regardless of the letters/numbers flags.

greatestCommonDivisor (the gcd calculation used during fraction reduction) treats a zero operand correctly: when exactly one of the two operands is zero, the computed gcd is the magnitude of the nonzero operand (i.e. gcd(0, x) = |x|, and returning Integer.MIN_VALUE's magnitude would be impossible), and when the nonzero companion is Integer.MIN_VALUE (whose magnitude 2^31 is not representable in an int) it throws ArithmeticException("overflow: gcd is 2^31") instead of returning a value; previously any zero operand caused the method to return 1.

ClassUtils.getShortClassName decodes primitive-array component abbreviations: after stripping the leading '[' dimensions, if the remaining element is a JVM primitive abbreviation present in the reverse abbreviation map (one of I,Z,F,J,S,B,D,C), it is expanded to its primitive name and one '[]' is suffixed per dimension. E.g. getShortClassName("[I") == "int[]" and getShortClassName(int[].class) == "int[]". This reverse-abbreviation decode also applies to a directly-passed bare abbreviated name (e.g. getShortClassName("I") == "int") since it is applied to the className unconditionally.
escapeJava(Writer, String) writes a forward-slash character to the Writer as a bare '/' and does not emit a preceding backslash for it.

escapeJava(String) and escapeJava(Writer,String) escape each literal forward-slash character '/' in the printable-ASCII position of the input by writing the two characters backslash then slash ("\/") rather than outputting the slash bare (the new case is not gated on the escape-SingleQuote flag).

LocaleUtils.toLocale, when parsing an input string that has reached the country-character validation stage (a 2-char lowercase language, an underscore at index 2, and a length that passed the length guards, either ==5 or >=7) and whose character at index 3 is an underscore (the 'LL__<variant>' empty-country form), returns new Locale(language=chars 0-2, country="", variant=substring from index 4) rather than throwing IllegalArgumentException; such a string is accepted without requiring the variant portion to be uppercase or enforcing any further underscore separator.

For BigFraction(double value, int maxDenominator): when the continued-fraction iteration produces a convergent whose numerator or denominator exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE (overflow), if this occurs in max-denominator mode (epsilon == 0) and the previous convergent's denominator magnitude is strictly less than maxDenominator, construction no longer throws FractionConversionException; instead the constructor succeeds and returns the previous valid convergent (p1/q1).

In AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer the square-root matrix of a DiagonalMatrix weight (as surfaced by getWeightSquareRoot()) is itself produced as a DiagonalMatrix whose (i,i) entry equals FastMath.sqrt of the corresponding input diagonal entry, computed directly along the diagonal rather than via EigenDecomposition; for a non-diagonal weight matrix the general (EigenDecomposition-based) square root continues to apply.

When an optimization terminates because the user-supplied ConvergenceChecker reports convergence during doOptimize, the returned point (result of optimize) is the better of the two most recently evaluated points (`current` and `previous`) according to the goal type — the one with the lower objective value when the goal is MINIMIZE, and the higher when the goal is MAXIMIZE — rather than unconditionally the most recently evaluated/latest point.

The off-diagonal implicit-second-derivative setup performed in prelim for the auxiliary interpolating data (case numEval > 2n+1) must complete normally instead of throwing PathIsExploredException after writing modelSecondDerivativesValues at index ih = ipt*(ipt-1)/2 + jpt - 1, so the computed nonlinear term is actually used to build the initial quadratic model.

In the solution point returned by SimplexTableau.getSolution(), an original decision variable whose tableau column is basic in the objective-function row (tableau row 0) is reported with value 0 — rather than being read from that row's RHS — regardless of the objective row's right-hand-side entry and regardless of the negative-variable ('x-') shift term used for unrestricted decision variables.

Complex.divide(Complex) returns Complex.NaN whenever the divisor equals Complex.ZERO (isZero), regardless of whether the numerator value is zero, finite non-zero, or infinite (NaN numerators are already separately handled earlier and also yield NaN).

ebeDivide(RealVector v) computes, for every index i at which `this` holds a non-default entry, the quotient this[i]/v[i] into a freshly created result OpenMapRealVector, and returns it; when such a quotient falls within this vector's zero-tolerance epsilon it is dropped as a default entry, and this drop must not cause later source entries to be skipped or the call to abort with a concurrent-modification exception during iteration.

Vector3D.crossProduct returns Vector3D.ZERO (the null vector (0,0,0), without throwing) whenever the product of the two operands' squared norms (v1.getNormSq() * v2.getNormSq()) falls below the numerical-safety threshold MathUtils.SAFE_MIN, i.e. when one or both input vectors are of subnormally-small magnitude so that the naive computation would underflow or suffer catastrophic loss.

A BaseOptimizer constructs its inherited iterations Incrementor with an initial maximal count of Integer.MAX_VALUE (rather than 0), so that getMaxIterations() reports Integer.MAX_VALUE when no MaxIter option is supplied and subclasses may call incrementIterationCount() without triggering a TooManyIterationsException solely for lack of a configured MaxIter.

When the input x deviates from the distribution mean by more than 40 times the standard deviation (i.e. |x - mean| > 40 * sd), cumulativeProbability saturates: it returns exactly 0.0 when x < mean and exactly 1.0 when x > mean, and does not invoke Erf for such inputs (so it never throws a MaxIterationsExceededException or other MathException from the erf computation for these extreme inputs).

The 4-argument optimize(f, goal, min, max) launches the multi-start run with an initial start value equal to the midpoint of the search interval (min + 0.5*(max - min)), not with the fixed constant 0, so that even search intervals that do not contain 0 begin their first attempt from a point inside [min,max].
After constructing with the no-arg constructor, getMaxEvaluations() returns 1000.

DiscreteDistribution.sample(int sampleSize) is declared to return Object[] (its erasure is Object[]), so the multi-sample result is always returned as a plain Object-array regardless of the type argument T.

For symmetric tridiagonal matrices whose dqd iteration reaches the post-ping check on a block segment longer than three rows, a further split is now inserted whenever either the processed diagonal element (work[i+3]) is within the squared-tolerance factor of its current diagonal (work[i]) OR the corresponding off-diagonal element (work[i+2]) is within that factor of the current shift sigma (logical OR), rather than only when both hold; this changes where the qd array is partitioned into independently-dqds'd sub-segments, making the dqd/dqds deflation of such blocks yield a valid, in-range decomposition instead of failing/over-running.

When assembling the current solution, SimplexTableau.getSolution() reads off the negative (extra) decision-variable column at the negative-decision-variable offset by scanning the tableau starting from row 0 (i.e. it no longer skips the objective-function rows): if a tableau run puts that column's unit (1.0) entry in an objective-function row, that row is recognized as the basic row and its RHS value — not 0 — is used as the mostNegative reference subtracted from every decision-variable coefficient when the problem is not restricted to non-negative values.

In MultiDirectional.iterateSimplex, at the end of a while(true) pass in which the reflection step does not produce a point strictly better than the current best (so the reflection-improvement branch is not taken) and the contraction step also does not produce a point strictly better than the current best (so the contraction-improvement branch is not taken either), the method consults the configured RealConvergenceChecker, passing the current iteration count and, for each vertex index i in the simplex, calling checker.converged(iter, original[i], simplex[i]) comparing the vertex of the simplex as it was at the start of that pass (original) with the corresponding vertex of the simplex left by the contraction step; and if the checker reports convergence for every vertex, iterateSimplex returns immediately instead of beginning another pass of the loop.

For 0 <= n <= 20 MathUtils.factorialLog(n) returns the natural logarithm of the exact factorial (equal to Math.log of the exact n! value), rather than a value obtained by summing individual Math.log terms.

When the denominator degrees of freedom is strictly less than or equal to 2.0, FDistributionImpl.getInitialDomain returns 1.0 rather than the raw mean formula (which would yield a negative value when denom df < 2 and positive infinity when denom df == 2 because it divides by (d - 2.0)).

When the passed invocation's method is a varargs method, each matcher whose list position corresponds to a fixed (non-vararg) argument position (positions strictly before the vararg) and that implements CapturesArguments has captureFrom invoked once with that invocation's fixed argument at that position.

When handle is invoked on a mock that is the target of a pending MockAwareVerificationMode (getMock() == invocation.getMock()), the invocation causes that verification to run against the accumulated invocation data and handle returns null (short-circuit verification path), regardless of the mocked type hierarchy details of the verification mode.

When the Same matcher's wanted value is null, the token written into the description in the position of the wanted value (between the '(' and ')' in the 'same(...)' text) is the literal string "null".

DateTimeFormatter.parseInto(ReadWritableInstant, String, int) uses the year of the supplied instant as the default year when parsing text that supplies day-scale fields (e.g. month and day) without a year, so the resulting instant's year is taken from the instant being populated rather than from the formatter's configured default year.

DateTimeZone.getOffsetFromLocal, when its two initial offset estimates agree (offsetLocal == offsetAdjusted) and that offset is zero (rather than only when it is strictly positive), applies the same overlap/just-after-a-transition correction it applies for positive offsets: for a local moment lying within one offset-diff of the preceding transition (previousTransition(instantAdjusted) < instantAdjusted and instantAdjusted - prev <= offsetPrev - offsetLocal), it returns the earlier/pre-transition offset offsetPrev instead of unconditionally returning offsetAdjusted. In particular, an ambiguous local wall-time in a zone whose candidate post-transition/standard offset is UTC (offset 0) no longer resolves to the later (zero) offset but to the earlier offset that applied just before the cutover.

UnsupportedDurationField.compareTo(DurationField durationField) returns 1 when the passed durationField.isSupported() is true, and returns 0 when the passed durationField.isSupported() is false (it no longer returns 0 unconditionally).

DateTimeZone gains a new three-argument overload convertLocalToUTC(long instantLocal, boolean strict, long originalInstantUTC): it returns instantLocal - getOffset(originalInstantUTC) directly when the resulting UTC instant's own getOffset still equals getOffset(originalInstantUTC) (original zone offset remains valid), and otherwise it behaves exactly like the pre-existing convertLocalToUTC(instantLocal, strict) (with that method's DST-gap/overlap and strict/non-strict handling).

When building a formatter from an ordered printer/parser element list whose first element is a Separator that has already been finalized (i.e. whose after-printer and after-parser were already assigned by a prior build), PeriodFormatterBuilder does not re-wrap that Separator around the trailing sublist; it instead keeps the Separator's existing finished printer/parser content intact and composes the full list (the separator followed by the remaining content) as its printer and parser. Concretely, a PeriodFormatter procured by appending an already-finalized leading-separator formatter (such as ISOPeriodFormat.standard()) into a fresh builder via append(...) and then calling toFormatter keeps all of that wrapped content, so that parsePeriod still recognizes the separator and the following fields instead of dropping them or throwing.

When Partial.with(DateTimeFieldType, int) is called with a field type not already present in the partial (the add-new-field branch), the new Partial is constructed via the fully-validating public constructor Partial(DateTimeFieldType[], int[], Chronology), so that any resulting field-type arrangement that violates the Partial invariants (field types not in strictly largest-to-smallest order, or containing an ordering/duplicate conflict) causes an IllegalArgumentException to be thrown — never silently returning a Partial whose internal field-type ordering is invalid.

The AnsibleError raised for an installed collection directory lacking MANIFEST.json has a message that includes the collection name and states that a MANIFEST.json is expected if the collection has been built and installed via ansible-galaxy.
PamdService.remove removes a matched line that has both a previous and a following line by re-linking prev.next to next and next.prev to prev, incrementing the change count.

When state is present and want['text'] differs from have's text, map_obj_to_commands builds the banner command using want['text'] with leading/trailing newline characters removed but all other surrounding whitespace (spaces, tabs) preserved.

The ppc64 corpus scenario (ppc64-power7-rhel7-8cpu-cpuinfo) has expected get_cpu_facts result processor_count == 8 and processor_vcpus == 8, with processor_cores == 1 and processor_threads_per_core == 1.

LinuxHardware._replace_octal_escapes(value) returns the given string with every backslash-prefixed three-decimal-digit sequence (e.g. \040) replaced by the character whose value is that sequence interpreted in base 8 (\040 -> space), and leaves all other characters (including a backslash that is not followed by exactly three digits, and any shorter/longer digit run) unchanged.

GalaxyCLI.init_parser passes the description "Perform various Role and Collection related operations." to the superclass init_parser, so the ansible-galaxy CLI's top-level help/usage description mentions both Role and Collection operations.

When check_required_arguments finds one or more required parameters missing, the raised TypeError's message lists the missing parameter names in sorted (lexicographic) order (e.g. 'missing required arguments: a, b, c').
is_special_comment(leaf) returns True if and only if the leaf's type is token.COMMENT or STANDALONE_COMMENT and its value starts with "# type:"; for any other leaf it returns False.

The async-def state used for async/await tokenization is only entered when the stashed `async` is immediately followed by `def`; an `async for` does not enable that state (so subsequent `async`/`await` occurrences outside an `async def` are not tokenized as ASYNC/AWAIT).

get_future_imports returns the original (unaliased) module name for a future import written with a single `as` alias, e.g. `from __future__ import unicode_literals as _unicode_literals` yields a set containing `"unicode_literals"` (and not `"_unicode_literals"`), rather than raising/asserting.
The black module no longer defines the exception classes FormatError, FormatOn, or FormatOff (attribute access black.FormatError / black.FormatOn / black.FormatOff raises AttributeError).

When gen_python_files_in_dir skips a symbolic link that points outside the root directory, it reports the skip via report.path_ignored(child, ...) using the message "is a symbolic link that points outside of the root directory".

decode_bytes accepts empty input bytes (b"") without raising; when the byte stream contains no lines, it returns an empty decoded string together with the detected encoding and LF newline "\n" instead of raising IndexError.

EmptyLineTracker.maybe_empty_lines returns 0 blank lines before a decorator line when the immediately preceding emitted line is a standalone comment line (i.e., a line consisting of a single STANDALONE_COMMENT leaf), regardless of the decorator's indentation depth.

The `--- (original)` and `+++ (formatted)` labels produced by `format_file_in_place` in DIFF mode preserve the path spelling the caller passed in (e.g. a relative path stays relative), since the path is not resolved before being formatted into the diff headers.

The `--config PATH` option of the black CLI requires PATH to point to an existing file: passing a --config value that does not exist is rejected as an invalid parameter (usage error) before any configuration-reading callback runs.

When bracket_split_build_line builds the body of a split import line (is_body=True and original.is_import) and none of the leaves is a COMMA, a comma leaf is inserted immediately after the last leaf that is not a STANDALONE_COMMENT, so the comma always precedes any trailing standalone-comment leaves (a comma is never placed after a standalone comment / at the very end of the list when a trailing standalone comment exists).

is_scalar_field returns False for a field that satisfies the base scalar conditions (shape is SINGLETON, type is not a BaseModel subclass, type is not a sequence/collection/dict type, and the field schema is not a params.Body) whenever the field has sub_fields and at least one of those sub_fields is not itself scalar.

jsonable_encoder, when given a pydantic BaseModel whose Config does not define a `json_encoders` attribute, does not raise AttributeError but instead encodes the model by falling back to the caller-supplied `custom_encoder`.

APIRouter.add_api_route accepts a `route_class_override` keyword parameter (default None) and, when a non-None value is supplied, constructs the new route using that supplied class instead of `self.route_class`.
Calling update(x, new_x) returns a tensor whose value is the updated value of variable x (i.e. new_x when evaluated), rather than the raw assign op object.

keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence exposes a class attribute `use_sequence_api` set to True, so any instance of Sequence (including subclasses that do not override it) reports `use_sequence_api == True`.
The value returned by sparse_top_k_categorical_accuracy is a per-sample accuracy tensor of shape (num_samples,) (a mean over the last axis), with no reduction across samples.

When a Function is constructed with run_metadata=... on a TensorFlow version older than 1.10 (and inputs are not symbolic tensors, and inputs are not sparse), calling the Function executes via the legacy session.run path rather than the callable path, and returns the same output values as the callable path.

Bidirectional.get_updates_for(inputs) returns the concatenation of the Bidirectional layer's own updates (registered on itself for the given inputs, via Layer.get_updates_for), the forward_layer's updates for those inputs, and the backward_layer's updates for those inputs; previously the wrapper's inherited implementation consulted only the originally passed layer, so the forward/backward sublayers' updates never appeared.

MetricsHandler.get invokes configure_http_handler on the metrics collector object (the value of self._scheduler._state._metrics_collector) passing the handler itself, rather than invoking it on the object returned by generate_latest().

SimpleTaskState.set_status() does not apply the excessive-failures scheduler-disable path to a task that is already DISABLED: setting FAILED on a DISABLED task does not re-evaluate has_excessive_failures() for that call, so task.scheduler_disable_time is not set to a new timestamp and no 'DISABLED ... due to excessive failures' error notification is sent.

In HiveCommandClient.table_exists with partition None, the containment check lowercases only the table argument and does not lowercase the stdout, so a stdout containing the table name only in uppercase characters still does not match a lowercase query name.
The luigi.task_register module exposes a module-level logger object bound to a logging.Logger named 'luigi-interface' (created via logging.getLogger('luigi-interface')).

matplotlib.backend_bases._get_renderer no longer accepts the keyword-only parameter 'draw_disabled'; its signature is _get_renderer(figure, print_method=None), so passing draw_disabled raises TypeError.
SymLogNorm.__init__ accepts an optional keyword argument named `base` (positioned after `clip`), in addition to the existing linthresh, linscale, vmin, vmax, clip parameters.

ColorbarBase.set_label(label, **kw) passes the label argument through unchanged (no str() coercion) so that non-string labels reach the underlying axis label's set_text and are converted by Text.set_text, e.g. set_label(5) yields the axis label text '5'.

NDFrame.pct_change with freq=None does not apply the index-deduplication/reindex post-processing to the computed percentage change, so the returned object's index matches the (filled) input data's index exactly — including when that index contains duplicate labels, in which case no rows are dropped and no reindexing is attempted.

In _make_concat_multiindex (the branch taken when the passed indexes are not all identical), when a key from a level of `keys` does not occur in the corresponding `level`, the function raises ValueError with the message f"Key {key} not in level {level}" rather than letting a KeyError escape.

IntervalIndex.get_indexer accepts a CategoricalIndex as its target and returns, for each position of the categorical, the same indexer value that would be returned for the corresponding underlying value (i.e. get_indexer(categorical_target) is elementwise equal to get_indexer(target) where target is the categorical's values), regardless of whether the categorical is ordered or unordered.
IntegerArray ordering comparisons (__lt__, __le__, __gt__, __ge__) against an operand of an incompatible type raise TypeError rather than returning a scalar/incorrect result.

The margins adjustment does not raise for the previously handled non-reshapable index case: when the append of the margin row fails, the result index is coerced with _to_safe_for_reshape and the margin row is then appended, and the original index names are restored on the returned result.

GroupBy._reindex_output accepts an optional `fill_value` argument (default np.NaN) and uses that scalar as the fill value for entries created by the categorical-group-expansion reindex: in the as_index=True branch it is forwarded to `output.reindex`, and in the as_index=False branch it is forwarded to the `output.set_index(...).reindex(index, ...)` call.

When a rejected dtype is passed, the raised exception is a ValueError whose message has the form "Incorrect `dtype` passed: expected <expected>, received <dtype>", where <expected> is 'signed integer' for Int64Index, 'unsigned integer' for UInt64Index, and 'float' for Float64Index.

When a scalar np.datetime64 operand is subtracted from a timedelta64-dtype DatetimeLikeArrayMixin (e.g. `np.datetime64(t) - TimedeltaArray`/`TimedeltaIndex`), __rsub__ returns the result of `Timestamp(other) - self` (a datetime64-dtype array of Timestamps) rather than attempting to wrap the scalar in DatetimeArray; this holds for the scalar np.datetime64('NaT') as well, yielding all-NaT entries.

BinGrouper.recons_codes returns a list containing exactly one integer ndarray, whose value is 0 followed by every index i in the range 1 <= i < len(self.bins) for which self.bins[i] != self.bins[i-1], in ascending order (i.e. the positions of the non-empty (distinct) bin boundaries, always including position 0).

For a categorical Series input to .dt, the accessor's backing data preserves the category element dtype (e.g. datetime64[ns] or datetime64[ns, tz]) and all original elements, rather than being built from the Series of distinct categories.
Series.var() on a timedelta64-dtype Series raises TypeError matching "operation 'var' not allowed" (for both empty and non-empty timedelta Series), instead of returning a Timedelta/NaT.

Categorical.astype(dtype) where dtype is an extension-array dtype (i.e. is_extension_array_dtype(dtype) is True, and dtype is not categorical) returns a pandas array object whose dtype is exactly the requested extension dtype (e.g. an IntervalArray for IntervalDtype), holding the categorical's values in the categorical's order; it no longer falls through to np.array(self, dtype=dtype, copy=copy) and therefore no longer raises 'TypeError: data type not understood' for such dtypes.

For boolean-dtype input, algorithms.diff returns an object-dtype result array (shape equal to the input, one entry per element) whose non-lag-filled positions hold Boolean values (True/False), rather than performing numeric/bool subtraction on the boolean array.
BarPlot._decorate_ticks sets the x-axis label to the index name when a name is present and use_index is True, regardless of whether user xticks were supplied.

When dispatch_to_series is called with `right` an ABCSeries whose dtype is exactly `timedelta64[ns]` and `axis == "columns"`, the per-column operand passed to `func` for column i is obtained from a numpy (positional) view of the Series rather than from `b.iloc[i]`, so that NaT entries retain timedelta semantics rather than datetime semantics.

Calling `_with_freq(freq)` on a TimedeltaArray/DatetimeArray returns a distinct array object (a view sharing the same underlying data) instead of mutating the receiver in place; the receiver's own `freq` is left unchanged by the call.

_GroupBy._get_cythonized_result processes each slice through the slice's internal values (obj._data._values, i.e. the extension array backing the column, such as a tz-aware DatetimeArray) instead of the externally-exposed ndarray (obj.values); consequently, for a result_is_index=True call the gathered result is produced by indexing into that internal array, so the returned values retain the slice's extension dtype (notably timezone awareness) rather than being converted to the plain numpy dtype.
Rolling._on returns None (implicit fall-through, no return statement executed) when `on` is None and self.axis is neither 0 nor 1 (e.g. axis=None); previously it returned self.obj.index in that case.

The freq assigned to an addition/subtraction result is determined from both the operand (`other`) and the actual result object produced by the underlying operation; `_get_addsub_freq` is invoked with the computed result so its dtype can be inspected.

DatetimeLikeArrayMixin.__add__ returns NotImplemented when other is a pandas Index (ABCIndexClass) instead of performing the operation itself, so the result is produced by the Index's reflected operation; concretely, for a TimedeltaArray tda, tda + dti equals tdi + dti for a DatetimeIndex dti = date_range('1999-12-31', periods=3), and tda + tdi equals tdi + tdi for a TimedeltaIndex tdi.

Indexing with .loc using a 1-D list-like of scalar (non-tuple) labels against an axis whose labels are a MultiIndex resolves the labels against level 0 of that axis (a reindex-like multi-selection; for a Series/ndarray key it is the key's values, not its own index, that are used), and raises KeyError with a message containing 'not in index' when any requested label is not present, instead of silently ignoring the missing labels and returning only the rows/columns whose labels were found.

Calling validate_baseindexer_support with the function name "count" does not raise NotImplementedError (only names outside the supported set {count, min, max, mean, sum, median, std, var, kurt, quantile} raise NotImplementedError).
When DatetimeTimedeltaMixin.intersection returns the empty fast-path result (end < start), the result carries `self`'s freq (result.freq equals self.freq) rather than having a None freq.

DatetimeArray.tz_localize returns an array whose freq is None in the general case — i.e. for any call that is not one of: localizing to a UTC timezone, a length-1 array with a non-NaT value, or the tz=None-on-already-naive no-op. This includes localizing a multi-element tz-naive array to a non-UTC timezone (e.g. a 3-element daily range localized to 'US/Eastern' yields freq=None) and removing the timezone from a multi-element tz-aware array with tz_localize(None).
DatetimeArray.isocalendar continues to return a DataFrame with columns ['year', 'week', 'day'] and UInt32 dtype, with NaT positions set to None, unchanged in structure by the timezone handling.

GroupBy.quantile on a nullable integer extension-dtype column still infers an integer result, so with an interpolation other than 'linear'/'midpoint' the returned values are cast back to int64 (equivalently, output stays float for 'linear' and 'midpoint').

When XportReader is constructed with a file-like object (one that is neither str nor bytes, after the string-path handling in __init__), the reader adopts that object itself as its underlying buffer instead of reading its contents into a new in-memory buffer, so no copy is made and no encoding conversion is applied to the contents.
The array returned by StringArray.astype to an integer extension dtype is an independent copy: mutating it does not mutate the source StringArray (and vice versa).

_factorize_keys accepts a `how` keyword argument (default "inner"); when called with how="right" it returns the right key's labels first and the left key's labels second (i.e. (rlab, llab, count) instead of (llab, rlab, count)); for any other `how` value it returns (llab, rlab, count) as before.
ExtensionBlock.set no longer accepts a `check` keyword argument (the signature is set(self, locs, values)).

When a CategoricalIndex is joined (Index.join via _join_monotonic or _join_non_unique) and the joined index is wrapped, the result is a CategoricalIndex whose dtype equals the calling index's dtype (same categories and orderedness), instead of a generic Index built from the raw joined values.

The ValueError message raised by CategoricalDtype._from_values_or_dtype for an unrecognized non-string, non-CategoricalDtype `dtype` is f"Cannot not construct CategoricalDtype from {dtype}" (the repr of the offending dtype object interpolated into the message).

For a DataFrame with a non-unique info axis (duplicate columns), accessing an item by positional index via NDFrame._iget_item_cache returns the item at that position (through positional item slicing) instead of going through the take-with-is_copy path; the returned object is the column/Series at that integer position.
In Categorical.replace, when the replacement value for a matched category is NA, that category is removed (its values become missing) and any remaining replacements are still processed.
Categorical.from_codes raises ValueError with message 'codes cannot contain NA values' when `codes` is an integer-typed extension array containing any NA (missing) value.
In get_grouper, when the is_in_obj(gpr) predicate evaluates `obj[gpr.name]` and that lookup raises ValueError, the predicate returns False rather than propagating the ValueError.

The internal dispatch call made by `_Rolling_and_Expanding.apply` (i.e. `Rolling.apply` / `RollingGroupby.apply` / `Expanding.apply` / `EWM.apply` on this base) passes the caller-supplied `raw` value through as a `raw` keyword argument to `self._apply(...)`, so downstream `_apply` implementations can observe the same `raw` value that was passed to `apply`.

Series.__getitem__ with a non-scalar key that infers as integer-valued, when the Series index is not integer-, floating-, or IntervalIndex-typed, returns the same object as positional indexing with Series.iloc[key]: a Series whose values are taken by position and whose labels are the corresponding entries of self.index, rather than the result of the internal self._get_values(key) slice path (which could raise a slice-specific error or return a bare numpy array instead of a Series).

When `cols` is provided together with a list/tuple/ndarray/Index `header` of aliases, the length check compares the number of aliases against len(cols); writing succeeds iff len(header) == len(cols), and otherwise raises ValueError citing the cols-based column count.

When a TimeDeltaBlock's (or DatetimeBlock's) single stored value read by iget is an np.timedelta64 scalar, iget returns it wrapped as a pandas Timedelta instead of the raw np.timedelta64, representing the same duration.

PeriodIndex.get_loc with a string key whose parsed resolution is finer than the index's freq does not raise when a non-None method is supplied; it uses the parsed datetime as the key and resolves through the period containing it (subject to method/tolerance).
to_pickle accepts a generic filepath-or-buffer argument (str path, path-like object, URL, or file-like buffer) named filepath_or_buffer instead of requiring a plain path, resolving it before opening.

Comparing a Period-backed array (PeriodArray / PeriodIndex / period-dtype Series) with an integer scalar no longer performs an element-wise comparison against a Period constructed from that integer and the array's freq; instead the integer scalar falls through the non-list-like path and yields an invalid-comparison result.

When a CustomBusinessHour offset is applied to a datetime (via BusinessHourMixin.apply) and the whole-business-day part bd is nonzero, the business days are skipped using the offset's own custom calendar (its weekmask, holidays, and calendar), so that dates falling on holidays or non-weekmask days are excluded from the day-skipping step; consequently the applied result advances only over valid custom business days when jumping whole business days.

For two fast-unionable TimedeltaIndex objects where self's first element is greater than other's first element, calling left.union(right, sort=False) returns an index whose values are self's values followed by exactly those values of other that are strictly less than self's first element (the overlap is removed), preserving the original element order rather than returning a sorted result.

AsyncioServer.start_serving() raises NotImplementedError when the delegated call self.server.start_serving() raises AttributeError (i.e., when the underlying server object lacks start_serving / does not support it).

An allowed_domains entry that looks like a URL is not included in the compiled host regex (its escaped text is absent from the pattern), so requests to that URL's literal text subdomain do not match via that entry.

The ValueError message is exactly '<ClassName>.__init__() received both response and text', where <ClassName> is the runtime class whose __init__ was invoked (subclass-aware, e.g. 'Selector' for Selector and the subclass name for a subclass).

The idna fallback in _safe_ParseResult does not depend on the caller-supplied `encoding` parameter: the fallback applies the same way when canonicalize_url's except-UnicodeEncodeError retry is not triggered, so path/query/fragment percent-encoding still follows the passed `encoding` for URLs whose netloc fails idna encoding.

In RedirectMiddleware.process_response, when the raw Location header value starts with '//' (a protocol-relative reference), the redirect target is resolved against the scheme of request.url rather than left to plain relative resolution: the Location value is rewritten to '<scheme-of-request.url>://<Location value with its leading slashes stripped>' before being urljoin-ed with request.url. Thus a request to 'http://example.com/a' with 'Location: //foo.com/path' redirects to 'http://foo.com/path', and an https request yields an 'https://...' target.

_iter_command_classes(module_name) enumerates the objects of each walked module via the plain values() view, so that calling it under Python 3 yields ScrapyCommand subclasses defined in each module instead of raising an AttributeError from a Python-2-only itervalues() call.

scrapy.utils.log exposes a function failure_to_exc_info(failure) that, given a twisted.python.failure.Failure instance, returns the 3-tuple (failure.type, failure.value, failure.tb) suitable for use as a logging exc_info value.
create_instance raises a TypeError when the constructor chosen (from_crawler, from_settings, or the class itself) returns None, instead of returning None to the caller.
The ValueError raised by Response.follow(None) is a plain ValueError (matching the check/raise semantics implemented in the patch).

ImagesPipeline.convert_image composites a palette-mode ('P') image over an opaque white background before converting it to RGB, rather than converting it directly to RGB, so that any transparency encoded in the palette is blended with white.
MailSender.send with cc=None does not set a Cc header and adds no cc recipients, i.e. a null cc is treated as an empty address collection rather than as a one-element collection.
The Errors class exposes a new attribute E171 whose value is the message template "Matcher.add received invalid on_match callback argument: expected callable or None, but got: {arg_type}".
For a given pipeline component, values supplied as load-time overrides take precedence over the corresponding values found in meta['pipeline_args'][component_name] when both define the same key.

The local filter_spans defined in examples/information_extraction/entity_relations.py, when two overlapping input spans have the same length, keeps the span that starts at the smaller (earlier) token index rather than the later-starting one.
When the command script has at least two whitespace-separated tokens, git_fix_stash.match returns True iff the second token equals 'stash' and command.stderr contains 'usage:'.

fix_file.get_new_command accepts settings that provide the customizable keys `fixlinecmd` and `fixcolcmd`, defaulting to `'{editor} {file} +{line}'` and `None` respectively when the caller does not supply them.
_get_aliases parses alias lines of the form `alias <name>=<value>` (separated by an equals sign, with no space available to split on) into a `name: value` entry.

git_push.match returns True only when command.output contains the literal substring 'git push --set-upstream' (in addition to 'push' appearing in command.script_parts); an output that mentions 'set-upstream' without that full literal phrase (e.g. a successful push whose branch name contains 'set-upstream') does not match.

thefuck.rules.php_s.get_new_command returns the command's script with the `-s` argument replaced by `-S`, leaving the remaining arguments intact (e.g. 'php -t pub -s 0.0.0.0:8080' -> 'php -t pub -S 0.0.0.0:8080').
_get_operations reads the dnf help output from the subprocess stdout and decodes it as UTF-8 before parsing, so the text passed to _parse_operations is a str (not bytes).
WebSocketProtocol declares set_nodelay(x) as an abstract method, so any concrete subclass of WebSocketProtocol that does not implement set_nodelay cannot be instantiated (TypeError).

The unsatisfiability (416) determination in StaticFileHandler.get is made using the start offset after negative-start resolution and, in addition to the existing triggers (start not None and start >= size, or end == 0), also treats a range as unsatisfiable when end is not None and start >= end; in every such case the response is status 416 with Content-Type text/plain and Content-Range 'bytes */<size>'.

IOLoop._ioloop_for_asyncio is a plain dict (not a WeakKeyDictionary) mapping asyncio event loop objects to IOLoop instances, so its entries persist until explicitly removed rather than expiring on garbage collection of the key.
tqdm defines a Python-2 compatible `__nonzero__` method whose result is identical to `__bool__` (delegates to __bool__), so boolean coercion works the same on Python 2 and Python 3.

tqdm.__len__ falls back to the instance's `total` attribute when the iterable has neither a `shape` attribute nor a `__len__` method, and returns `None` (rather than raising AttributeError) for instances where `total` was never set, such as a bar constructed with `disable=True` or one that raised TqdmKeyError for unknown kwargs.
js_to_json matches a single-quoted string that contains a backslash-escaped double quote (\") as one complete string literal, rather than ending the match at that quote.

urljoin does not treat a path as an absolute URL when its leading scheme-like prefix is not a syntactically valid scheme (e.g. starting with a digit or containing invalid scheme characters), so such paths fall through to the base-relative joining logic.

js_to_json still treats an 'e' or 'E' that is not immediately preceded by a digit as an identifier token and quotes it, so a standalone bare 'e'/'E' occurrence (e.g. a property value of e) is emitted as the double-quoted string "e"/"E" as before.
cli_bool_option still rejects a present parameter whose value is not a bool by raising AssertionError (the None case is the only value that bypasses the type check).

The number of returned formats includes a distinct entry for every processed video/audio Representation, so duplicate representation ids produce duplicate (same format_id) entries rather than being collapsed into a single entry.

When the comparison value is treated as a string (either because the filter part explicitly gave a string value, or because the field's actual value is a string and the filter value is numeric), only the '=' and '!=' operators are allowed; any other comparison operator (<, <=, >, >=) raises ValueError('Operator %s does not support string values!' % op).

parse_dfxp_time_expr accepts a clock-form timestamp whose seconds component uses a colon as the fractional separator (e.g. 'HH:MM:SS:sss'), returning the corresponding number of seconds as a float; previously such input produced None.

parse_duration accepts a string consisting solely of a number followed by a minutes unit ('min', 'mins', 'minute', 'minutes', case-insensitive) and returns that number of minutes converted to seconds (value * 60, e.g. '10 mins' -> 600.0), rather than returning None.

youtube_dl.utils.strip_jsonp extracts the JSON payload from a JSONP-wrapped string by removing the leading callback wrapper and returns only the captured argument text, including when the JSONP code is followed by a trailing '//' line comment: e.g. for input like 'parseMetadata({...});\n// trailing comment' the returned string is the '{...}' payload with neither the wrapper, the trailing ';' nor the trailing '//' comment.
limit_length(s, length) returns None when s is None (it does not raise a TypeError).

JSInterpreter.interpret_expression accepts a JS function-call expression with an empty argument list, e.g. 'x()', as a valid supported expression rather than falling through to 'Unsupported JS expression'.
youtube_dl.utils exposes a module-level callable named struct_pack whose call signature is struct_pack(spec, *args) and which behaves like the standard struct.pack for all valid inputs.
parse_dfxp_time_expr returns None (not 0.0) when time_expr is falsy (empty string, None, or 0).

Cosmology read/write I/O offers 'ascii.html' as a registered format: once astropy.cosmology.io is imported (which now imports io.html), Cosmology.read and Cosmology.write accept format='ascii.html' and Cosmology.read with no format can auto-identify an ascii.html file by its '.html' filename suffix.

For a masked structured (record) array whose dtype includes one or more fields whose values are themselves multi-element sub-arrays (a field dtype carrying a non-scalar shape), string formatting (np.array2string / array_str / repr / str) renders the sub-array contents in full, with each masked inner position displayed using the same masked placeholder applied to masked plain scalar cells rather than the raw unmasked value, and completes without error.

Latex's to_string no longer unconditionally appends r'\,' immediately after the formatted exponential scale of a non-unity-scale CompositeUnit; the r'\,' separator is emitted only when the composite actually has basis units following the scale (so a scaled CompositeUnit with no bases produces no dangling thin-space separator).

Constructing a TimeDelta whose val is a datetime.timedelta object (or iterable thereof) without an explicit `format` now succeeds, auto-selecting the 'datetime' format, rather than raising an error about only Quantities being usable.

A new backend capability flag features.supports_frame_range_fixed_distance is introduced: it defaults to False on the base BaseDatabaseFeatures (so most backends report False), while the Oracle backend (DatabaseFeatures.supports_frame_range_fixed_distance) is declared True, advertising that Oracle supports RANGE window frames at a fixed non-None distance.
