When USE_TZ is enabled and the requested timezone name differs from the connection timezone and encodes a fixed offset via an inline '+' or '-' sign (a datetime.timezone-style name), the CONVERT_TZ target argument is reduced to just the signed-offset tail starting at that sign (e.g. 'UTC+05:00' -> '+05:00', sign kept as written), rather than passing the full name, so that MySQL interprets the fixed Unicode offset; datetimes converted to a fixed-offset timezone thereby reflect that nominal offset. Names lacking such an inline sign are used unchanged.

ModelChoiceField.to_python accepts a value that is already an instance of the queryset's model by extracting the value's to_field_name attribute (defaulting to the model's pk) and using that extracted value for the queryset lookup; this resolves to the cached DB object rather than raising an invalid_choice ValidationError as was the case when the model instance itself was passed as the lookup parameter.
When the UserCreationForm's model USERNAME_FIELD is present in self.fields, that field's widget renders with the attribute autocomplete="username" (in addition to its retained autofocus="").

When register() is called on a model that is already in the registry and whose existing registration entry's admin object string representation ends with '.ModelAdmin' (i.e. the model was registered with a plain default ModelAdmin), it raises AlreadyRegistered whose message is exactly "The model <ModelName> is already registered in app '<s>'. " where <s> is that string representation with the trailing '.ModelAdmin' removed (e.g. the plain ModelAdmin's module path such as django.contrib.admin.options).

If accessing the URLconf module (get_resolver().urlconf_module) at reloader startup raises any Exception, the error is swallowed and reloader startup continues: the autoreload_started signal is still sent and the reloader's poll loop still runs instead of the exception propagating.

When a relation column is the table's primary key (a PK-FK column), inspectdb generates the field definition as a OneToOneField rather than a ForeignKey, preserving the explicit `primary_key=True` parameter and still including `models.DO_NOTHING` (e.g. `models.OneToOneField(InspectdbPeople, models.DO_NOTHING, primary_key=True)`).

When ServerHandler.cleanup_headers() runs for a response and the server that served it is not a socketserver.ThreadingMixIn instance (i.e. a non-threaded HTTP server), the 'Connection' header is set to 'close' even if the response does include a 'Content-Length' header, so the request handler's connection is marked for closing (close_connection becomes True) and a subsequent request is not kept alive on that connection.

When django.utils.http.urlencode is called with queries whose direct mapping value for a key is None (the outer loop guard, regardless of doseq), the TypeError raised has message "Cannot encode None for key '<key>' in a query string. Did you mean to pass an empty string or omit the value?", where '<key>' is replaced with the offending key.

In generated compound SQL, the per-operand parenthesization that is otherwise applied when the backend feature supports_slicing_ordering_in_compound is enabled is emitted only when the compound query is not itself a nested subquery: when a combined query is rendered as the subquery of an enclosing query (self.query.subquery is True), its top-level combined operands are not additionally wrapped in parentheses that a standalone combined query on such a backend would receive.

The security.W019 deploy-check warning message text is changed: when XFrameOptionsMiddleware is present in MIDDLEWARE and X_FRAME_OPTIONS is not 'DENY', the reported warning now reads "You have 'django.middleware.clickjacking.XFrameOptionsMiddleware' in your MIDDLEWARE, but X_FRAME_OPTIONS is not set to 'DENY'. Unless there is a good reason for your site to serve other parts of itself in a frame, you should change it to 'DENY'." — it no longer contains the sentence "The default is 'SAMEORIGIN', but".

make_template_fragment_key no longer URL-encodes vary_on values before hashing: characters that urllib.parse.quote would percent-encode (such as ':', '/', '%', whitespace, or non-ASCII characters) now contribute to the fragment-key MD5 digest in their raw string form, so the returned 'template.cache.<fragment>.<digest>' differs from the old percent-encoded-digest for such inputs.

When the rhs value supplied to an isnull lookup is not a bool instance (True or False), compiling that lookup (IsNull.as_sql) emits a RemovedInDjango40Warning carrying the message 'Using a non-boolean value for an isnull lookup is deprecated, use True or False instead.'; a bool rhs (True or False) does not emit any such warning.

When a database connection's settings are prepared for testing, if the TEST sub-dictionary does not already specify a 'MIGRATE' key, that key is set to the default value True in the connection's TEST settings (in addition to the existing CHARSET/COLLATION/NAME/MIRROR defaults, which remain None).

The django.db.models.query_utils.InvalidQuery exception class is retained but deprecated: evaluating isinstance(obj, InvalidQuery) returns True when obj is an instance of django.core.exceptions.FieldDoesNotExist or FieldError (as well as for actual InvalidQuery instances), and every such isinstance evaluation emits a RemovedInDjango40Warning deprecation warning with a message indicating InvalidQuery is deprecated in favour of FieldDoesNotExist or FieldError.

django.views.debug.technical_500_response now selects its response body format by Accept-header content negotiation: if request.accepts('text/html') it returns an HTML traceback with content_type='text/html' and status_code; otherwise it returns a plain-text traceback with content_type='text/plain; charset=utf-8'. The choice no longer depends on the X-Requested-With (is_ajax) header.

When generating its result via reverse(), FlatPage.get_absolute_url() first attempts the candidate url self.url.lstrip('/') (self.url with all leading slashes removed) before the unchanged self.url, so that a stored url conventionally written with a leading slash (e.g. '/about/') is reversed with that leading slash removed (the '<path:url>' converter cannot begin with '/'); when such a url is reverseable, the returned URL reflects the stripped (no leading slash) form.

CommandError instances expose a `returncode` attribute whose value is 1 by default and can be set through a `returncode=` keyword argument to the constructor; this applies to every CommandError (and, via inheritance, to subclasses such as SystemCheckError that do not override __init__).

The django.core.checks.Tags class provides a built-in tag member 'staticfiles' whose value is the string 'staticfiles', allowing system checks to be registered to, and filtered by, the staticfiles tag.

When the configured session engine's SESSION_ENGINE module exposes a SessionStore whose clear_expired() raises NotImplementedError, running/executing the clearsessions command raises django.core.management.base.CommandError whose message is exactly "Session engine '<SESSION_ENGINE>' doesn't support clearing expired sessions.", causing the command to fail (non-zero return code) rather than writing a message to stderr and completing normally.

If a FilteredRelation's relation_name itself fails to resolve to a plain chain of relationship fields (i.e. solving it leaves leftover lookup/transform segments), add_filtered_relation raises ValueError with message 'FilteredRelation\'s relation_name cannot contain lookups (got %r).' identifying the offending relation_name.

When the state for a model instance is produced by Model.__getstate__, FK/related-value entries already present in the source instance's ModelState.fields_cache are carried over as copied entries into the returned state's copied fields_cache (rather than being dropped or shared by reference), so a shallow copy or unpickled copy of an already-populated instance retains its prior cached related values independently of any later mutations to the original's cache.

When update_fields names a field(s) not in the validated non-primary-key concrete-field set, Model.save raises ValueError whose message enumerates the offending fields as not existing, being m2m, or being non-concrete fields ('The following fields do not exist in this model, are m2m fields, or are non-concrete fields: <comma-separated names>') rather than the prior text that omitted the non-concrete-field clause.

When SessionBase.decode is given session data whose signing.loads decode raises signing.BadSignature AND whose legacy decode path (_legacy_decode) also raises an exception, decode does NOT propagate an exception: it logs a warning 'Session data corrupted' to the 'django.security.SuspiciousSession' logger and returns an empty dict {}.

TemplateView.get passes the keyword arguments it receives from dispatch (URLconf-captured URL kwargs) directly into the template context, so each URL keyword argument name maps in the rendered context to its ordinary raw value, no longer wrapped in a lazy/deferred object.

On the SQLite backend, an exact-equality filter on a JSON member against one of the JSON literals true, false, or null (field__key=True / field__key=False / field__key=None) selects exactly the rows whose stored JSON value at that key equals that JSON literal, and does not additionally match rows storing a different JSON literal or an integer of equal SQL value, or rows lacking that key.

When binascii.Error data cannot be successfully decoded by the legacy fallback (e.g. the unsigned payload is not valid legacy JSON), CookieStorage._decode returns None and marks the storage as used rather than raising an exception.

When CursorDebugWrapper.debug_sql emits a query-log entry to the 'django.db.backends' logger, the rendered debug message text appends the database connection's alias to the existing '(duration) sql; args=params' format, i.e. the message ends with '; alias=' followed by the connection alias (self.db.alias) after the args component.

ManyToManyField.check() (via the _check_ignored_options machinery, wired through ManyToManyField.check and model-level check) returns a django.core.checks.Warning with id 'fields.W345', message 'related_name has no effect on ManyToManyField with a symmetrical relationship, e.g. to "self".', and obj set to the field, whenever the field's remote_field.symmetrical is truthy and a truthy related_name was explicitly supplied to the constructor (self._related_name). Conversely, no such W345 warning is emitted when either no related_name was explicitly supplied or the relationship is not symmetrical.

While generating an AddField operation for an added field, if the (default-adjusted) field being added is unique, has a default that is not models.NOT_PROVIDED, and has a callable default, MigrationAutodetector calls questioner.ask_unique_callable_default_addition(field_name, model_name) for that field; when any of those three conditions is false the hook is not invoked for that field.

The squashmigrations management command refuses to run when the on-disk destination migration file it would write already exists: instead of creating/overwriting any file at that path, it fails the command by raising CommandError whose message contains the phrase 'already exists' and the new migration name.
MultiWidget.id_for_label(id_) returns the empty string '' for every argument, so that a field-level <label> associated with a MultiWidget never points (via for=) to its first subwidget's HTML id.

Calling path() or re_path() with a kwargs argument that is not None and not a dict raises a TypeError whose message indicates the kwargs argument must be a dict and names the actual type passed (e.g. '...but got str.') instead of proceeding to build the pattern/resolver.
The migrate management command accepts a --prune command-line option (stored as the 'prune' option).

For a ResolverMatch whose func is the callable produced by a class-based view's View.as_view() (i.e. func has a `view_class` attribute, with the wrapper's `__name__` left as 'view'), ResolverMatch stores `_func_path` as the wrapped view class's fully-qualified dotted path `view_class.__module__ + '.' + view_class.__name__` (e.g. `app.views.LazyRedirectView`) instead of the wrapper callable's own path `func.__module__ + '.' + func.__name__` (which would be `app.views.view`). As a consequence, `ResolverMatch.__repr__` prints `func=<module>.<ClassName>` for such class-based views, and when the matched pattern has no url_name its `view_name` components the same class path.

Calling CryptPasswordHasher's constructor (instantiating the class) emits a RemovedInDjango50Warning with message 'django.contrib.auth.hashers.CryptPasswordHasher is deprecated.' before normal base-class initialization proceeds.

When the autodetector generates an AddField for a field on an app/model and the same-change computation also removes a field of that identical name from that model (so the field name must be dropped then re-created, e.g. a ForeignKey/concrete field being replaced by a plain ManyToManyField), the resulting set of migration operations orders the re-adding AddField strictly after the matching RemoveField of that field name — never before it — so a single combined migration can apply both without relying on incidental list order.

When BaseDatabaseWrapper.on_commit is invoked with robust=True while the connection is in autocommit with no atomic block in progress (so func runs immediately), an exception raised by func is caught and logged instead of being propagated out of the on_commit call, which returns normally; when robust=False (the default), an exception from func propagates out of that immediate on_commit call unchanged.

Supplying name (and optionally violation_error_message) as positional arguments to the constraint constructor, i.e. the legacy form BaseConstraint('name'[, 'message']), now emits a RemovedInDjango60Warning deprecation warning.

URLField.to_python (and therefore URLField.clean) prepends the field's configured scheme (self.assume_scheme) rather than a hard-coded 'http' to scheme-less URL inputs, so the scheme prepended to a scheme-less value such as 'example.com' is whatever scheme the field was constructed with.

When a StepValueValidator is constructed with a non-None offset and the value fails the step check, the raised ValidationError conveys code "step_size" with the offset-aware message text ("starting from %(offset)s, e.g. %(offset)s, %(valid_value1)s, %(valid_value2)s, and so on.") and params limit_value, offset, valid_value1 (= offset + limit_value), and valid_value2 (= offset + 2*limit_value).

When removing such a shared Axes, the surviving sibling's minor formatter is left untouched if its owning axis treats it as a default (isDefault_minfmt True), i.e. a default minor formatter is preserved rather than re-set/cleared.

During automatic legend handle collection, a candidate artist (including a .Text) whose label is neither empty nor '_nolegend_' but for which no legend handler can be found in the effective handler map is no longer silently discarded; it triggers an external warning of the form "Legend does not support handles for {ConcreteTypeName} instances." pointing to the legend_guide 'implementing-a-custom-legend-handler' section, and that artist is NOT emitted as a legend handle.

When tripcolor is called with neither a positional C argument nor a 'facecolors' keyword (facecolors is None and no positional arg remains after the triangulation spec is consumed), it raises a TypeError (not ValueError) whose message is "tripcolor() missing 1 required positional argument: 'C'; or 1 required keyword-only argument: 'facecolors'".

A constructed Legend instance exposes a public instance attribute `legend_handles` whose value is the list of Artist objects actually added as legend-handle entries (one per retained legend entry, in the same order and aligned with `legend.texts`); the list is reassigned at the end of `_init_legend_box` to the finalized `handle_list`, and it is precisely the list that `get_lines`, `get_patches`, and the labelcolor color-getter loop read from.

In the mesh-data setup shared by pcolor/pcolormesh (Axes._pcolorargs), the number of rows and columns of the mesh is derived from the first two dimensions of C only, so C with more than two dimensions (notably 3D RGB(A) image data of shape (M,N,3) or (M,N,4)) is accepted rather than raising an unpacking error; the mesh is laid out on an M×N grid of the leading dims.

Changing a LineCollection's alpha (set_alpha) while it has a gapcolor set re-applies the gap color converted with the updated alpha, so the value returned by get_gapcolor() thereafter reflects the new alpha.

Calling grab_frame(savefig_kwargs=...) where savefig_kwargs contains the key 'dpi', 'bbox_inches', or 'format' raises a TypeError (rejected before the frame is saved), because those arguments are controlled by the MovieWriter.

Request.register_hook continues to store a hook value that is not a list, tuple, or set (e.g. a single callable) as a single entry appended to self.hooks[event], preserving single-hook registration semantics.

"nanoseconds" is a recognized unit in TIME_UNITS, so netCDF timedelta variables whose attrs units == "nanoseconds" are decoded (CFTimedeltaCoder.decode takes the decode path and yields a numpy timedelta64[ns] array) instead of being returned undecoded.

In the plain-text repr of a DataArray or Variable (array_repr), when display_expand_data is False the data is rendered as the single-line inline_variable_array_repr summary instead of the (possibly multi-line) short_data_repr value shown when the option is True or left at 'default'.

duck_array_ops.is_duck_array (utils-level utility is_duck_array): an object that has ndim, shape and dtype attributes and implements __array_namespace__ counts as a duck array even when it does NOT provide both __array_function__ and __array_ufunc__; previously such an object was NOT a duck array.

AbstractArray.__format__ invoked with a non-empty format_spec on an array-valued (shape != ()) object raises NotImplementedError with a message stating that using format_spec is only supported when shape is () and reporting the actual shape.

Converting to a pandas.Index an xarray Variable or DataArray whose underlying data is a pandas MultiIndex stored at a particular level (i.e. a MultiIndex level coordinate, such as a named level 'one' of a stacked dimension) yields a single-level, non-Multi pandas.Index of that level's values repeated per position, rather than the underlying full pandas MultiIndex of row tuples.

When the global keep_attrs option resolves to True, the Dataset returned by a non-inplace binary operator (e.g. ds1 + ds2) has its dataset-level .attrs overwritten with the left operand's (self.attrs); when the option resolves to False (the default), the result's dataset-level .attrs are left as produced by _calculate_binary_op (i.e., not taken from the left operand).

Calling enable/disable/disable_next on a PyLinter with a *numeric* message id (accompanied by a resolvable symbol and a non-empty module/current_name) appends a ManagedMessage(name, msgid, symbol, line, is_disabled) record to that PyLinter's own instance attribute `_by_id_managed_msgs` (initialized in __init__). The by-id managed-message state is now per-linter-instance rather than residing in a class-level list shared by MessagesHandlerMixIn, so two distinct PyLinter objects keep independent such records.

Two BaseChecker instances are equal (×==× returns True) if and only if the string formed by concatenating the first checker's name and the string form of its msgs dict equals the analogous concatenation for the second checker; otherwise ×==× returns False. (Because the class defines no __eq__ prior to this patch and is decorated with @functools.total_ordering, this value equality also governs the total-ordering-derived comparisons, so checker ordering is now likewise based on this name+msgs value rather than object identity.)

If the same option source (a configuration file or the command line) supplies both an enable/disable option that covers 'all' (value with a comma-separated element exactly 'all') and the opposite all-action option — i.e. both an '--enable=all'-type/--enable for all and an '--disable=all'-type/--disable for all — pylint raises pylint.config.exceptions.ArgumentPreprocessingError with the message '--enable=all and --disable=all are incompatible.' instead of silently choosing an order.

The default value of the TfidfVectorizer.dtype parameter is np.float64 (rather than the integer np.int64 dtype inherited from CountVectorizer), so a TfidfVectorizer constructed without an explicit dtype stores dtype=np.float64.
Passing any explicit (non-None) axis value to the Imputer, including 0 or 1, causes fit to emit a DeprecationWarning announcing that 'axis' is deprecated in 0.20 and will be removed in 0.22.

TfidfVectorizer.idf_ is writable: assigning an iterable of IDF weights to vectorizer.idf_ propagates them to the inner TfidfTransformer so that they become readable via vectorizer.idf_ and are used for weighting in transform(), overriding the need for them to be learned by fit().
Calling KNeighborsMixin.kneighbors with an explicit n_neighbors argument that is less than or equal to 0 raises a ValueError reporting the offending n_neighbors.

When copy_Xy is False but the supplied Xy array is not writeable (e.g. read-only or memmap-backed), _gram_omp no longer raises an error from its in-place coefficient-swapping; it makes an internal copy of Xy and returns the same coefficients it would have produced if Xy were writeable.

Calling fit on an IsolationForest whose contamination == 'legacy' emits a FutureWarning stating that the default contamination value 0.1 will change to 'auto' in version 0.22 and that this will change the predict method behavior.

After `fit`, SimpleImputer sets an `indicator_` attribute: when add_indicator=True it is a fitted sklearn.impute.MissingIndicator instance constructed with the imputer's own `missing_values` placeholder and trained on the fit-time data; when add_indicator=False it is None.

In check_array, an input object that exposes both a `dtypes` attribute and an `__array__` attribute but whose `.dtypes` is empty or has no length (e.g. a pandas Series holding a single scalar dtype) is accepted and validated through all the normal conversion/validation/warning steps without crashing on a 0-d iteration; in particular it no longer records `dtypes_orig` from that `.dtypes` attribute, so it does not enter the end-of-function multiple-original-dtypes DataConversionWarning comparison path regardless of `warn_on_dtype` and any resulting dtype difference from the converted array.

When the true targets scored are of type 'continuous-multioutput' (multi-column continuous y), calling score first emits a FutureWarning whose message states that the default value of multioutput (not exposed in the score method) will change from 'variance_weighted' to 'uniform_average' in version 0.23 to keep consistent with metrics.r2_score; when the targets are single-output continuous, no such FutureWarning is emitted.

Passing a discrete_features string that is not 'auto' (or that is not ExactlyEqual to the literal 'auto') raises a ValueError with message 'Invalid string value for discrete_features.', instead of being treated as a boolean-like or index-like value.

When `stratify` is supplied as a 2-dimensional (e.g. multi-label) array, resample supports stratification by treating each distinct row of stratify as a separate class (each row mapped to a single joined-string identifier), so that the per-row class proportions are approximately preserved in the drawn sample rather than failing or stratifying per individual column cell.

When analyzer is a callable and input is 'file' or 'filename', calling build_analyzer triggers a one-time validation probe in which the callable analyzer is invoked on the string name of a file that does not exist; if that invocation raises FileNotFoundError, or raises AttributeError with message "'str' object has no attribute 'read'", a warning classified as ChangedBehaviorWarning whose message begins 'Since v0.21, vectorizers pass the data to the custom analyzer...' is emitted; for any other outcome (the callable returns successfully or raises some other exception) no such ChangedBehaviorWarning is emitted and the exception is swallowed without propagating.

When VarianceThreshold.fit is called with the default threshold of 0.0 on sparse (CSR/CSC) input, any feature column whose samples are numerically constant across all rows is given an effective variance of 0 (self.variances_ = min(mean_variance_axis result, min_max_axis-derived range) = 0), so that the feature is dropped rather than being kept due to a floating-point residual variance.

When a scalar Number `sample_weight` (with `sample_weight is not None`) is passed to BaseDecisionTree.fit, fit no longer raises; instead the estimator fits with that constant weight applied equally to every sample (i.e. equivalent to equal weighting).

When an iterable fed to sklearn.utils.parallel.Parallel.__call__ contains a delayed function that does not support config attachment (e.g. one created with joblib.delayed instead of sklearn.utils.parallel.delayed), a UserWarning is raised stating that sklearn.utils.parallel.Parallel must be used in conjunction with sklearn.utils.parallel.delayed rather than joblib.delayed to correctly propagate the scikit-learn configuration; the task still runs without an attached shared config.

Calling MLPClassifier.partial_fit or MLPRegressor.partial_fit (stochastic solver 'adam'/'sgd') on an estimator whose early_stopping parameter is True raises a ValueError with message "partial_fit does not support early_stopping=True", rather than continuing training. This applies regardless of whether the model was previously fit with early_stopping (which would leave best_loss_ = None) or is a first partial_fit call, and it occurs before validation-set splitting / weight initialization of the incremental pass.

kmeans_plusplus now exposes a new keyword-only parameter `sample_weight` (array-like of shape (n_samples,), default None, versionadded 1.3); when provided it is validated against X via _check_sample_weight (a malformed weight — e.g. negative values or length != n_samples — raises), and non-None weights are propagated into the private weighted seed-selection routine.

RocCurveDisplay.plot renders a legend at location 'lower right' whenever a label is present in the main ROC line's kwargs OR in the chance-level line's kwargs (so that when plot_chance_level=True the 'Chance level (AUC = 0.5)' line is always included in the legend); it renders no legend only when neither curve carries a label.

When the configured language is exactly 'en', Sphinx performs no catalog searching, mo-file compilation, or translator population from locale dirs (the translator is initialized with an empty locale list) and logs none of the 'loading translations...'/'done'/'not available for built-in messages' messages.

At import time of sphinx.addnodes, SIG_ELEMENTS contains exactly the standard signature leaf node classes desc_sig_space, desc_sig_name, desc_sig_operator, desc_sig_punctuation, desc_sig_keyword, desc_sig_keyword_type, desc_sig_literal_number, desc_sig_literal_string and desc_sig_literal_char, each of which is declared as a desc_sig_element subclass with _sig_element=True.

Description-typehints mode is driven by the autodoc_typehints config value staying equal to 'description' during the build (it is no longer internally rewritten to 'none' by a config-inited handler); description rendering no longer depends on any separately set runtime flag.
The mathjax_path configuration value, when not explicitly set by the user (i.e. left at its default), defaults to the string 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js'.

The viewcode extension no longer inserts pending_xref nodes of reftype 'viewcode' into the doctree; nevertheless, any such pending_xref still reaching the missing_reference handler is resolved into a source reference link as before, and resolving one of these legacy nodes emits a RemovedInSphinx50Warning deprecation warning.

Setting up the `sphinx.ext.autodoc` extension now also sets up the `sphinx.ext.autodoc.preserve_defaults` sub-extension, which registers on the Sphinx application a configuration option named `autodoc_preserve_defaults` whose default is `False`.

During cross-reference resolution, when a pending_xref node contains a pending_xref_condition child matching 'resolved' first, or otherwise matching '*', the content element (contnode) handed to domain xref resolvers and to the 'missing-reference' event is derived from that matched condition's child content (preferring 'resolved' over '*') rather than from the raw first child of the pending_xref node; if no such condition child is present, it is derived from node[0] as before.

Every pending_xref node produced by type_to_xref now carries a refspecific attribute (its value is True exactly when the incoming target began with a leading '.', and False otherwise); because PythonDomain.resolve_xref treats mere presence of the refspecific attribute as enabling refspecific search, all type-annotation cross-references emitted through type_to_xref (e.g. from py:data/py:attribute/py:property ':type:', function return/parameter annotations) are now resolved in refspecific search mode (module/class-context and suffix-based lookup) rather than the default exact-match mode even when the target is not prefixed.

LaTeX printing of a FormalPowerSeries (e.g. the object returned by fps(f)) renders the series' infinite Closed-form representation s.infinite — the Add of the independent terms plus an unevaluated \sum (sigma) over the general term ak.formula * xk.formula running from k=ak.start to infinity — instead of the truncated finite polynomial expansion returned by s.truncate(). Concretely, latex(fps(f)) now contains an infinite Sum over the coefficient/general term and no longer trails the truncated 6-term expansion with a \mathcal{O}(...) order term.

LatexPrinter._print_SingularityFunction emits the SingularityFunction with its exponent rendered as a braced superscript group `^{<power>}` directly after the closing `>` of the angle-bracket expression, with no space between caret and exponent, so that exponent values that contain a leading minus sign or are multi-character (e.g. -1, -2) produce valid output rather than being split off by whitespace from the caret (e.g. latex(SingularityFunction(x, 0, -1)) equals r'{\langle x \rangle}^{-1}', not r'{\langle x \rangle}^ -1').

Matrix.is_upper_hessenberg evaluates to True for a rectangular matrix having more rows than columns whose entries that lie in the strictly-below-subdiagonal band within the matrix's actual columns are all zero — in particular an all-zero k×m matrix with k > m reports is_upper_hessenberg == True rather than raising an IndexError from iterating a column index ≥ cols.

When expr is an Add expression and separate=True, decompose returns a Python set (unordered, duplicate-free) whose elements are the constituent monomials of expr (one per Add term), instead of a list.

For an Add or Mul instance whose `as_independent(Symbol, AppliedUndef)` yields a non-identity numeric part x and a non-trivial tail (the "pure number" path of AssocOp._eval_evalf), `_eval_evalf(prec)` returns the freshly-constructed flat expression `self.func(x, e1, e2, ...)` where each `ei` is the individual result of that tail argument's own `_eval_evalf(prec)` (the original tail argument kept when its `_eval_evalf` returns None); this reconstruction is performed unconditionally on every call, rather than only when the per-tail-argument evaluations actually changed something.

The simplify() signature is changed so that the former fourth keyword parameter `fu` is removed and replaced by a new keyword `rational` (default False), i.e. the signature is simplify(expr, ratio=1.7, measure=count_ops, rational=False); consequently a call that passes an explicit `fu=...` keyword now raises TypeError and a call passing `rational=...` (True, False, or None) is accepted.

exptrigsimp no longer accepts a 'simplify' keyword argument; its signature is now exptrigsimp(expr), so a call passing a simplify= flag is a TypeError, and the transformation set it applies to its input is no longer conditional on such a flag (the one library caller, top-level simplify(), which formerly disabled this, now invokes the full transformation).
rcode / RCodePrinter translates a factorial function expression into an R call 'factorial(...)' of its argument, rather than reporting it as not supported.

The negative-base, negative-exponent simplification in both Rational._eval_power and Integer._eval_power no longer branches on whether the negative exponent is an integer (expt.q == 1): a single representation is returned for all negative non-unit exponents, with the sign factored as (-1)**expt using the untransformed negative exponent.

When logcombine collapses a group of log terms sharing a common coefficient factor k into the single logarithm log(combined), where combined is produced from the same logcombine routine over the product of the terms' (coefficient-raised) arguments, that resulting single logarithm is constructed with automatic evaluation disabled, so that it is stored back into the combination table in an unevaluated form rather than already auto-simplified; this prevents the intermediate combined log from being prematurely evaluated (for instance when the grouping reduces to a form involving numeric/log content that autoevaluation would absorb or alter) before the opposite-signed-coefficient division recombination of the same pass can act on it.

ConditionSet's third argument base_set is optional, defaulting to S.UniversalSet, so ConditionSet(sym, condition) (with no base set) constructs a ConditionSet whose .base_set is S.UniversalSet instead of raising a TypeError.

binomial(n, k) auto-evaluates to n when n - k equals 1 (i.e. k == n - 1) and n is known to be nonnegative or a non-integer; in particular, binomial(n, n - 1) now evaluates to n for a positive-integer symbol n instead of remaining unevaluated.

FCodePrinter (e.g. via fcode) raises NotImplementedError when asked to print a SymPy Mod / % expression while the 'standard' setting is 66 or 77 (the raised message states that Python's % operator and SymPy's Mod() are not supported by Fortran 66 or 77); since the default 'standard' is 77, a plain fcode(Mod(...)) now raises.

LatexPrinter now prints a HadamardPower (elementwise matrix power) matrix expression instead of falling through to a generic constructor-style print: the base is printed with the standard power-handling used for ordinary x**n superscripts and the exponent is shown as an elementwise (ring)∘ marker, yielding output of the form `{base}^{\circ {<exp>}}` (e.g. a bare MatrixSymbol base printed as `A^{\circ {2}}`).

When Factors is constructed from a general Expr (a non-atom, non-pure-Number product expression) whose resulting powers-dict contains a key f that is a non-Integer Rational p/q with exponent e (=factors[f]), the construction no longer keeps that Rational entry in Factors.factors; instead Integer(p) is entered/accumulated with exponent +e, Integer(q) is entered/accumulated with exponent -e, and the Rational key f is removed.

For a Segment3D or Ray3D argument whose intersection with the plane is empty (the entity does not reach the plane), Plane.distance returns the Euclidean distance from the plane to the nearest point actually on that bounded/ray entity rather than the perpendicular plane-to-point distance to that entity's first defining point regardless of its extent: for a Ray3D this is the plane-to-point distance of the ray's initial point o.p1, and for a Segment3D it is the plane-to-point distance of the nearer of the two endpoints.

count_ops counts operations across both the keys and the values of dictionary input: a Python dict is sympified to a Dict and then processed via the Dict path summing count_ops of each key and each value, and a SymPy Dict input is likewise processed over its key/value items (rather than only over its keys via generic iteration).

In Mul.matches, when the pattern (self) and the expression are both non-commutative products, the commutative (scalar) factors are separated from the non-commutative factors and matched among themselves first; a side whose product has no scalar factors is treated during that step as if it had the scalar factor 1.
A sign expression whose argument is known to be zero under the assumptions refines to 0 (IntegerZero / S.Zero).

Under evaluation-disabled context (evaluate(False)), adding (or the reflected add of) oo or -oo with any Number operand no longer collapses to the eager infinite/NaN result (nan/oo/-oo); instead it produces an unevaluated Add expression (e.g. Add(oo, -1) rather than oo).

When evaluating a reciprocal power (Pow(b, e))**other with e == -1 (i.e. an inner exponent of -1) and with `other` having a rational form whose denominator is literally 2 (the `_half` case), a base b that is known to be non-negative (b.is_negative is False) is simplified directly to `Pow(b, -other)` (i.e. b**-other) — e.g. computing (b**-1)**Rational(m,2) for such a b reduces to b**Rational(-m,2).
dup_zz_mignotte_bound returns the non-negative even integer bound; for the polynomial `f = x**3 + 14*x**2 + 56*x + 64` over the integer domain ZZ it returns exactly 152.

Rendering a SingularityFunction that itself carries an outer exponent (a powered SingularityFunction, i.e. one printed through the LaTeX Pow path that supplies an `exp`) does not raise an error and yields the wrapped LaTeX form `{\left({\langle SHIFT \rangle}^{POWER}\right)}^{EXP}`, where SHIFT is the rendered argument-difference (args[0]-args[1]), POWER is the rendered internal exponent (args[2]), and EXP is the rendered outer exponent.

Constructing a symbolic Range collapses it to the canonical empty range (start=stop=0, step=1, i.e. Range(0)) whenever the computed member count (stop-start)/step is exactly 0 (start and stop symbolically equal) or is negative (a symbolically-descending or vacuous span), rather than merely detecting the trivial start==stop case.

Mul.is_integer reports False (not None/undecidable) for products where the remaining (post-±1-removal) numerator factors are all odd while at least one denominator factor is even, and for forms having a single even numerator Integer whose combined factor-of-2 content from the even denominators strictly exceeds the numerator's own factor-of-2 count.
In the cgs_gauss unit system, the scale factor of ampere is set to 10*speed_of_light*statcoulomb/second.
Multiplying two Prefixes whose scale factors are reciprocal (scale product == 1) yields S.One (a SymPy Integer equal to 1) rather than the bare Python integer 1, e.g. m*k == 1 still holds.

_line_type recognizes the missing-value token 'NO' and the 'nan' data token case-insensitively during line classification: a row consisting of multiple NO tokens in any letter case (e.g. 'no no no no') is still classified as 'new' (a table separator), and a data row whose values include NO/nan in mixed or lowercase casing (e.g. '1.2 no' or 'NAN') is classified as a data line of the correct column count rather than rejected as unrecognized.

_format_float(value) always returns a string of length at most 20: when the base representation exceeds 20 characters and contains scientific notation ('E'), only the leading mantissa characters are dropped so the retained prefix plus the intact 'E' exponent portion totals 20 characters; when the base representation exceeds 20 characters and contains no 'E', the first 20 characters are returned.

When Quantity is constructed from an existing Quantity input (no unit change) with dtype=None and copy=True, an integer-kind input Quantity is promoted to float64, whereas a float16 (or other float-kind) input Quantity keeps its original float dtype instead of being widened to float64 — only integer-kind inputs trigger the float default in this code path.

When an Aggregate (e.g. a Count) is compiled to SQL with distinct=True, the rendered function arguments contain the keyword DISTINCT followed by whitespace, so it is separated from the leading source expression rather than being concatenated directly onto it (an expression whose SQL starts with a keyword- or identifier-like token, such as a CASE, previously merged with DISTINCT into a single invalid token). When distinct=False, no DISTINCT is emitted.

DatabaseClient.runshell_db launches psql via subprocess.run with check=True, so a non-zero exit status of psql propagates as a CalledProcessError (i.e. the call does not silently swallow psql failures).

Under Oracle, when USE_TZ is enabled, _convert_field_to_tz (used by datetime_cast_date_sql, datetime_cast_time_sql, datetime_extract_sql, and datetime_trunc_sql) treats the stored datetime field as being in the connection's configured timezone: when self.connection.timezone_name differs from the requested tzname the SQL takes the field as being in the connection timezone (FROM_TZ source = self.connection.timezone_name, replacing the fixed '0:00' UTC offset) and converts it to tzname, and when the two timezones are equal the field is returned unchanged without any conversion.

In django.utils.numberformat.format, the zero-normalization applied to Decimals smaller than the decimal_pos cutoff discards the sign: a Decimal with magnitude below the cutoff produces the unsigned string (e.g. format(Decimal('-1e-200'), '.', decimal_pos=2) yields '0.00' with no leading minus), because the value is reset to a positive Decimal zero before the sign/negative handling.

django.utils.html.escape(text) returns a SafeString whose content is the input str(text) with HTML-significant characters encoded, namely: & becomes &, < becomes <, > becomes >, " becomes ", and ' becomes '.

The cached hostname exposed by django.core.mail.utils DNS_NAME (CachedDnsName) is returned in punycoded ASCII form: get_fqdn() returns punycode(socket.getfqdn()) and __str__() yields that same ASCII form, so a non-ASCII system hostname is rendered as its `xn--` ACE label while an ASCII hostname is returned unchanged.

replace_unnamed_groups replaces an unnamed capture group that terminates the regex pattern at its very end (its closing ')' is the last character, with no following literal token, including nested groups such as '((x|y)\w+)') with '<var>'. E.g. '^(?P<a>\w+)/b/(\w+)' is returned as '^(?P<a>\w+)/b/<var>' and '^(?P<a>\w+)/b/((x|y)\w+)' as '^(?P<a>\w+)/b/<var>'.

Every Choices class created through ChoicesMeta — including Choices, IntegerChoices, TextChoices, and any user-defined subclass of these — gets a class attribute 'do_not_call_in_templates' whose value is True (i.e. it is set when the class is created, not merely inherited through MRO lookup).

The flush management command calls connection.ops.execute_sql_flush with only the sql list (no database-alias argument), so the flush is performed on the connection bound to the --database option's alias.

When autodetecting changes, if a newly created model's base is given as a dotted string 'app.Model' and that base model is present in both the from_state and to_state project states, and the base model has removed a field (the field name is present in the old base model state's fields but not in the new base model state's fields) whose name is also redeclared among the newly created model's own fields, then the generated creation is made dependent on the removal of that same-named base field (a removed-field dependency on (base_app_label, base_model_name, field, False)).

DecimalField.to_python, when the non-None, non-float value it is converting via decimal.Decimal(value) causes a TypeError or ValueError (in addition to the already-handled decimal.InvalidOperation) — e.g. a dict, list, or other unsupported input — raises a django.core.exceptions.ValidationError with the field's 'invalid' error message, code='invalid', and the offending value in params, rather than letting the raw TypeError/ValueError propagate.

Query.clone() (invoked whenever a QuerySet is chained/cloned, including the clone QuerySet.none() makes before it sets the query empty) produces independent clones of each of the source query's combined_queries sub-query objects rather than sharing references to them, so that mutating a clone's combined sub-queries (e.g. recursively emptying them via set_empty) does not alter the source combined queryset's constituent sub-queries.

HttpResponseBase.delete_cookie forces Secure on the deletion cookie (in addition to the pre-existing __Secure-/__Host- name-prefix logic) when the given samesite value is 'none' (case-insensitive), so that a cookie previously set with SameSite=None can actually be deleted by a browser.

When get_limit_choices_to() resolves to a falsy value (such as None or an empty mapping/dict), apply_limit_choices_to_to_formfield does not restrict the queryset — the form field keeps its original unfiltered queryset.

The email appended to the hashed value is taken from the email field resolved via user.get_email_field_name() (cls.EMAIL_FIELD, defaulting to 'email'), so on a custom user model whose EMAIL_FIELD names a different attribute, it is that attribute's value whose later change invalidates the token.

When `__main__.__spec__` is None or its `parent` is falsy (i.e. the process was not launched as a package via `-m`), get_child_arguments() does not add any ['-m', ...] entry and instead falls through to script-path handling: it returns [str(<sys.argv[0] with .exe suffix>)] + sys.argv[1:] if that .exe exists, [sys.executable] + warning options + [str(<sys.argv[0] with '-script.py' suffix>)] + sys.argv[1:] if that script exists, appends full sys.argv (including argv[0]) when sys.argv[0] exists, and raises RuntimeError('Script %s does not exist.' % sys.argv[0]) when sys.argv[0] does not exist.

The `-m` relaunch branch is now selected based solely on __main__.__spec__ being present (not None); it is no longer additionally gated on a truthy __main__.__spec__.parent, so when __spec__ exists but parent is empty the child is still relaunched via `python -m <name>` rather than falling through to the script-file path.

BaseDatabaseClient.runshell invokes the client executable via subprocess.run with env=None (so the child inherits the calling process's os.environ) whenever settings_to_cmd_args_env returns a falsy env value such as an empty dict, instead of passing that empty dict/env to the subprocess.

settings_to_cmd_args_env() resolves the database name for the mysql CLI from settings_dict['OPTIONS']['database'] when present, falling back to settings_dict['OPTIONS']['db'] and then to settings_dict['NAME'] (i.e. the OPTIONS 'database' key is now accepted as an alias); when the resolved value is non-empty it is appended as the final positional (database) argument in the returned command args.
QuerySet.bulk_update() called with an empty collection of objects (objs with no elements, after all field/pk validation has passed) returns the integer 0 rather than returning None.

When BaseFormSet.full_clean() runs and no formset-level ValidationError is caught (including when the formset is unbound / management form is invalid / all checks pass), the non-form error list it produces and that formset.non_form_errors() returns is an ErrorList whose error_class is 'errorlist nonform', so rendering it as HTML (as_ul()/str()) emits '<ul class="errorlist nonform">'.
django.utils.timezone._get_timezone_name(tz) returns the result of tz.tzname(None) when that call yields a truthy (non-None, non-empty) string, and otherwise falls back to returning str(tz).

get_language_from_path() recognizes a path whose initial language-prefix segment is a code of the form word('-word|@word){0,2} — i.e. comprised of up to three subtags joined by single '-' or '@' (e.g. en-latn-us, zh-hant-tw) — extracting that whole three-subtag code as the candidate language code; for a path prefix representing a supported language (present in LANGUAGES and with a matching locale file), it returns the corresponding supported language variant instead of None. (Previously only one- and two-subtag prefixes such as en, en-us, pt-br could be parsed; a three-subtag prefix such as en-latn-us caused the code not to be extracted.)

Query.bump_prefix accepts an optional `exclude` iterable of aliases; when supplied, those aliases are left unchanged (not relabeled to the newly chosen prefix), while all other aliases are renumbered to fresh aliases under the new prefix. When `exclude` is None (the historical calling convention), every alias is relabeled as before.

ForeignKey.db_parameters(connection) returns a dict that, in addition to 'type' and 'check', contains a 'collation' key whose value is the value returned under 'collation' by the foreign key's target_field.db_parameters(connection).

When.as_sql: when the condition compiles to an empty SQL string (a filter that matches every row, e.g. a negated empty lookup like ~Q(pk__in=[])), the CASE WHEN branch is emitted with an always-true predicate as its condition instead of a malformed/empty condition — so the WHEN's THEN result is returned for every row.

A `%` (MOD connector) CombinedExpression whose operands are an Integer output field and a Float output field (in either order) no longer raises FieldError during output-field resolution; its inferred output type is FloatField.

A constraint whose `violation_error_code` is not None is deconstructed (and thus cloned) with that `violation_error_code` included in kwargs, so `clone()` reproduces the non-default code; the kwarg is omitted when the code is None (the default).

SelectDateWidget.value_from_datadict does not raise OverflowError when the submitted year/month/day values are integers that cause datetime.date(int(y), int(m), int(d)) to raise OverflowError (rather than ValueError); instead it returns the string "0-0-0".

In Query.get_aggregation, when any aggregate expression being resolved references an existing annotation whose underlying expression reports contains_over_clause (i.e. a window-function annotation such as one built with django.db.models.Window), the query is routed to the wrapped-subquery aggregation path: the row-level (window) computation is performed in an inner query and the aggregate is applied over its results in the outer query, rather than inlining the window expression directly inside the aggregate in a single SELECT. Observable effect: a QuerySet such as .annotate(<window alias>).aggregate(<Aggregate of that alias>) executes without producing invalid or incorrect SQL and returns a value equal to applying the aggregate to the per-row window values.

For a method bound to a class nested inside an enclosing class/namespace, the serialized output must include the complete nesting path (all enclosing dotted segments) so the emitted expression names the actual class, and the 'import <module>' for that class's module is still emitted.

In _ImageBase._make_image, when norming resampled 2D image data whose norm is a LogNorm, if the recomputed/un-scaled vmin (s_vmin) is less than or equal to 0, that vmin is set to np.finfo(scaled_dtype).eps (the smallest representable positive float of the scaled dtype) before the norm is invoked, so that the norm is never handed a vmin of 0 or negative. Consequently a render whose round-tripped vmin is exactly 0 succeeds (the previous code only corrected strictly negative vmin and would pass vmin==0 through, causing the log-norm application to fail on that boundary).

When _wrap_in_tex converts its input text into TeX math-mode wrapping (used for usetex-rendered date tick labels), every colon ':' character that survives the earlier letter-classification step is braced as '{:}' in the returned string, so that time separators are not typeset with the wide spacing TeX gives to binary/relation operators.

When drawedges=True on a filled Colorbar that has no lower extension (_extend_lower() false), no divider is drawn at the lower vmin extreme — dividers there are only drawn if such a lower extension exists; likewise _extend_lower()/start_idx still starts cutting the interior below the lowest interior box boundary when no lower extension is present.

In ConciseDateFormatter.format_ticks, when the finest tick level whose values vary across the given ticks is at the year (level 0) or month (level 1) field, the offset is now forcibly suppressed (so no offset string is shown/offset_string stays empty) only if the set of distinct values taken by that field across the ticks includes the value 1 (e.g., a January tick when months vary); when those varying values do not include 1, the offset is kept displayed (show_offset stays on) even though the varying level is a year/month level.

AnnotationBbox.draw invokes renderer.open_group with self.__class__.__name__ as the group title (no type name string literal required beyond that source constant being reflected) before drawing its children when it proceeds past the visibility/xy guards.

When contourf()/QuadContourSet (filled=True) is drawn from a Z whose dtype is boolean and no contour levels are supplied, automatic level selection uses levels [0, 0.5, 1], so the resulting cs.levels equal [0, 0.5, 1].

Colormap.__call__ converts a non-float input X (an array whose dtype kind is not 'f', e.g. integer/unsigned/bool kinds) into a native signed integer dtype before substituting the over-range (self._i_over), under-range (self._i_under), and bad (self._i_bad) sentinel indices, so those substitutions always act on a signed buffer large enough to hold values self.N, self.N+1, and self.N+2. As a result, invoking a colormap on such an input -- including on an empty array such as np.array([], dtype=np.uint8), for which the sentinel indices self.N+2, self.N+1, self.N exceed the uint8 range when self.N=256 -- completes without emitting NumPy conversion/out-of-bounds (deprecation) warnings.
A Grouper instance whose _mapping holds weak references to live, weak-referenceable objects can be pickled (and unpickled, e.g. via pickle/copy.deepcopy) without raising an error.

When `.subfigures(ncols>1, wspace=w, ...)` is called on a Figure or SubFigure whose layout engine is None (get_layout_engine() returns None) and an explicit non-None wspace is passed, the bounding boxes of the returned column subfigures are adjusted so that a horizontal separation is left between adjacent columns (the grid cells are shrunk to accommodate the wspace gap) rather than every column adjoined flush against the next at the grid width-ratio boundary.

Collection.set_paths(paths) no longer raises NotImplementedError: it records the passed argument as the collection's paths (so that a subsequent call to the inherited get_paths() returns exactly the passed value) and marks the collection stale.

Blueprint.__init__ raises ValueError with message "'name' may not be empty." when its name argument is falsy (e.g. an empty string), rather than allowing the Blueprint to be constructed only to misbehave later during registration/endpoint generation.

When the keep_attrs argument of Variable.quantile is left at its default (None/omitted), whether or not the result retains the calling Variable's attrs is governed by xarray's global 'keep_attrs' option consulted via _get_keep_attrs with a default of False, mirroring the behavior of other Variable reduce methods.

Indexing a DataArray by label through .loc with a dict-like key (e.g. da.loc[{dim: label}]) returns the DataArray produced by selecting on those dimension labels, treating every dict key as a dimension/coordinate to look up rather than as a Python keyword argument — so this works correctly even when a dimension (or a key in the indexers dict) is named 'method', 'tolerance', 'drop', or 'indexers', which are reserved parameter names of DataArray.sel.

In the same case (data dtype kind 'u' and `_Unsigned` == "false"), if a `_FillValue` is present in the variable's attrs, that fill value is cast as the corresponding same-width signed integer type (e.g., an itemsize-1 fill value of 255 becomes -1).

xr.where(cond, x, y, keep_attrs=True) where y is a Dataset and x is not a Dataset (x is promoted so the result is a Dataset): the result's top-level .attrs is set to {} (not to x.attrs), and the data variable of the result named by x.name, if x has a name present in the result's data_vars, is given x's attrs.

When the PYLINTHOME environment variable is not set, the home directory resolves to a real path (USER_HOME is not "~"), and the legacy directory os.path.join(USER_HOME, ".pylint.d") already exists on disk, importing pylint.config prints a message to stderr stating that PYLINTHOME is now the new cache directory while the obsolescent old .pylint.d directory was found and can be safely removed (this is an existence check only — it does not create or delete the old directory).

The help/usage text for the `--verbose` (`-v`) and `--enable-all-extensions` command-line options renders those flags with no argument value/metavar placeholder token following them (their per-option metavar is the empty string, threaded through the _CallableArgument conversion and add_argument call), instead of the default dest-derived uppercase placeholder.

expand_modules._is_ignored_file normalizes the given element path with os.path.normpath before deciding whether it is ignored, so an element whose literal text only matches an ignore-rule once redundant '.'/'..' segments, non-canonical separators, or trailing path separators are resolved is still treated as ignored: after the fix, an element path that does not literally match an ignore-paths regex (ignore_list_paths_re) but whose normalized form does is reported as ignored (previously it was not).

LogCaptureHandler.clear() empties the handler's list of captured records (the records attribute holds an empty list after the call, having had all previously accumulated records removed) and resets the handler's captured text stream so that its previously formatted output is discarded.

fowlkes_mallows_score returns a correct Fowlkes-Mallows score (a value in the expected range, not corrupted by integer overflow) even when the contingency counts are large enough that the product of the two squared row/column sums (pk·qk) would exceed the range of a signed 64-bit integer; specifically the returned value is computed without ever forming that overflowing product.

When the search is run with a falsy `refit` (i.e. `refit=False`), calling fit does not create a `refit_time_` attribute on the instance, so the attribute is absent after fit (accessing it raises AttributeError).

The function sklearn.decomposition.dict_learning() accepts a new keyword `method_max_iter` (default 1000) that is propagated as the `max_iter` of the sparse_encoding lasso solve performed in each dictionary-update step.

HuberRegressor.fit accepts an input feature matrix X whose dtype is non-float (e.g. integer or boolean/categorical data stored as bool), casting it internally to a floating-point dtype and fitting successfully, so that calling fit does not raise a TypeError originating from numpy operations on the non-float array and the resulting model behaves equivalently to one fit on the same data converted to float64/float32.

In modify_field_list, for every object type (class or otherwise) under autodoc_typehints_description_target == "all", when an 'rtype' field is appended its body paragraph text is exactly the recorded return-annotation string ('annotations['return']'), not the value of any other annotation.

Catalog.__iter__ yields Message objects whose locations list is sorted ascending by (source, line) — ordered lexicographically by source path and then by line number for a given source (previously the locations were in the insertion order of the underlying metadata entries).

When Sphinx parses a type annotation into cross-reference nodes (via sphinx.domains.python._parse_annotation, reached from both signature parameter annotations via _parse_arglist and return annotations via handle_signature), any bare-name text equal to the literal string 'None' is turned into a pending_xref node with refdomain='py', reftarget='None', and reftype='obj', so that 'None' is referenced as a Python object/data rather than as a class.

DocstringSignatureMixin._find_signature recognizes an object's docstring signature when it is not located on the very first line of the object's docstring text: it scans the lines of each docstring block (skipping non-signature and empty lines) until it finds a signature whose base name matches the documented object, and treats the first such match as the signature.

Subscripting a _MockObject instance with a key of any type (not only str; e.g. an int, a type, or another non-string object) returns a new _MockObject subclass rather than raising an error, and the name of the resulting subclass is derived from str(key), i.e. the resulting subclass's __display_name__ equals the enclosing mock's __display_name__ + '.' + str(key).

For a class documented under an alias name (doc_as_attr), ClassDocumenter.get_doc returns an empty (non-None) docstring list when the class's real module source contains a module variable doc-comment for the alias name, and returns None when no such source comment exists. Consequently the alias is subjected to docstring processing (inherited autodoc-processing/autodoc-process-docstring applies to an empty docstring) only in the commented case, while an uncommented class alias still yields None and so performs no docstring processing.

When either the required extension version or the loaded extension's declared version is not a valid PEP 440 version string (packaging.version.Version raises InvalidVersion), verify_needs_extensions falls back to plain (lexicographic) string comparison between the required and loaded version strings to decide whether the requirement is met, raising a VersionRequirementError iff the required string is lexicographically greater than the loaded string.

Permutation.__new__ still rejects array-form entry containing repeated elements by raising ValueError('there were repeated elements.'); the repeated-element rejection is now applied only when the permutation is not in cyclic form.

When coth is evaluated on an Add argument for which _peeloff_ipi returns a nonzero periodic part m whose coth(m) is the singleton S.ComplexInfinity, evaluation returns coth(x) where x is the peeled rest, rather than raising an exception.

In the generic Set._complement method, when the minuend argument (`other`) is a FiniteSet, elements of that FiniteSet for which the subtrahend (`self`) reports definitive containment (`self.contains(el)` evaluates to true) are removed from the result; elements the subtrahend reports as definitively-not-contained (`self.contains(el)` evaluates to false) are retained and constitute the ordinary FiniteSet members of the returned set.
polylog(0, z) auto-evaluates to z/(1 - z) for any z for which it is not already caught by the z=1, z=-1, or z=0 branches.

When the first factor of a MatMul being LaTeX-printed is a negative number, output is a leading '-' followed by the space-joined rendering of the product obtained by using the absolute value of that coefficient with the remaining factors, so the negative coefficient is pulled out as a unary minus (e.g. MatMul(-1, A, B) renders as '-A B' rather than '-1 A B').

Printing a Lambda object now renders its body expression (both in the single-bound-variable form 'Lambda(<v>, <body>)' and the multi-variable form 'Lambda((...), <body>)') through the printer, so symbols in the body (e.g. under python(...)) are collected and declared, whereas previously only multi-variable argument lists were printed via _print and the body was raw-formatted.

Printing an unevaluated Min expression (an object whose top-level func is Min, with more than one argument that Min does not collapse to a single symbol/numeral) via mathematica_code / MCodePrinter yields Mathematica function-call bracket notation of the form 'Min[arg1, arg2, ...]' rather than the parenthesized python-call form 'Min(arg1, arg2, ...)' that CodePrinter's fallback dispatch produces.

In the Add branch of _sqrt_match, the shortcut that delegates the expression to split_surds (returning split_surds' [a, b, r]) is taken only when the square of every addend is Rational AND positive; an Add whose addends' squares are all Rational but with at least one square non-positive (zero or negative) no longer takes that shortcut.

Left multiplication of a Point by a scalar factor (`factor * point`) yields a new Point whose coordinates are each the factor multiplied by the corresponding coordinate of `point`, sympified and simplified (i.e. behaves exactly the same as the corresponding right multiplication `point * factor`), rather than falling through to a generic SymPy Mul expression.

Float.__eq__ returns Python False when the right operand sympifies to a Boolean (S.false/S.true, or Python bool False/True via _sympify), regardless of the Float's value — in particular a zero-valued Float no longer short-circuits through 'not other' and so no longer compares equal to S.false.

split_super_sub still applies its trailing-digit exception when the given base name consists of one or more alphabetic characters immediately followed by a run of one or more digits: those trailing digits are removed from the returned name and prepended as the first element of the returned subs list. The alphabetic-prefix character condition is now Unicode-letter based ([^\W\d_], i.e. any non-digit, non-underscore word character), so the exception also fires for names whose letters include non-ASCII/Unicode characters (e.g. Greek), not just ASCII a-z/A-Z.

Mod.eval no longer propagates a PolynomialError raised by the internal gcd(p, q)/gcd_terms simplification step: when gcd(p, q) on the dividend/divisor arguments raises PolynomialError (e.g. piecewise-related generator issue), evaluation catches it, treats the extracted common factor G as 1 so that no gcd reduction is applied, and continues with the remainder of the Mod.eval simplification, ultimately returning a valid Mod result (an evaluated result or an unevaluated Mod form) instead of raising.

The zeros of the imaginary part im used to identify real members of an ImageSet are computed from the factors of numer(im) (the numerator when im is treated as a rational expression), so that real-valued members correspond to roots of that numerator; a purely rational/fractional form of im is reduced by its numerator rather than treated by its compounded-as-given factors.

When PythonCodePrinter (and its subclass MpmathPrinter, both built atop AbstractPythonCodePrinter) prints a Min expression, the result is a call to the Python builtin min with the Min's arguments as comma-separated operands (i.e. code string of form `min(...)`), instead of the previous rewrite-to-Piecewise/`# Not supported` fallback.
